articles.title: UEF, IIT-M join hands for Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026; focus on 10 key sectors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The United Economic Forum (UEF) Chamber of Commerce has signed an MoU with the Indian Institute of Technology - Madras (IIT-M) to collaborate for the Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026 scheduled to be held on December 8, 2026. The objective of this MoU is to facilitate knowledge sharing, industry academia collaboration, innovation, investment and stakeholder engagement towards Tamil Nadu’s economic growth.

The event will focus on 10 sectors, including Automotive & EV; Electronics & Semiconductors; IT, AI and Digital; Advanced Engineering & Capital Goods; Textiles & Technical Textiles; Pharma, Biotech & MedTech; Agri & Food Processing; Renewable & Green Energy; Logistics, Ports & Global Trade and Aerospace & Defence. Professors from the IIT-M ecosystem will lead each of these sectors.

V.Kamakoti, IIT-Madras Director through a video message said: “IIT Madras, and IIT Madras Research Park, and all our ecosystem are very happy to be associated with UEF to launch this Tamil Nadu Conclave 2026 as we march towards a multi-trillion economy.”

Mr. Kamakoti further said: “There are 10 highly emerging and extremely important from a societal angle verticals that have been identified, all the way from automotive, EV, electronics, semiconductor, IT, AI, technical, textiles, pharma, agri, renewable, green energy, aerospace, defense, logistics, and advanced engineering and capital goods.” He added, “And in each of these verticals, we are going to talk not just about the products, but also the supply chain, the logistics that is involved, the raw materials that are involved to make these, because many of them are deep tech technologies.”

Jinnah Rafiq Ahmed, Chairman, UEF – Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026 and Executive Chairman and Managing Director, Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited (KICL), said that a few MoUs would be inked at the conclave. To a query on whether investments are moving out of Tamil Nadu, he said that a lot of companies want to come to Tamil Nadu.

“Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth will be there, will continue and it will be unimaginable. Definitely, Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth will be very aggressive in the coming years. An industry from Tamil Nadu going out of State will not happen. And if it is, it might be an additional project in other States,” he said.

Ahmed A. R. Buhari, President — United Economic Forum (UEF) said, “Tamil Nadu has set an ambitious target of becoming a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036. UEF’s Unnatha Tamizhagam vision aspires to contribute towards Tamil Nadu becoming a $4 trillion economy by 2047.” The United Economic Forum in association with Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited and Airtel Business is organising the Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026.

articles.title: Panjab University improves its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The 2027 edition of the rankings, produced by Times Higher Education in association with Schmidt Science Fellows, assessed 1,058 institutions across 102 countries and territories, compared with 911 institutions in the 2026 edition

Chandigarh-based Panjab University (PU) has improved its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research, climbing 24 places to secure the joint 150th position in the Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027. The University’s overall score has increased to 55.0 from 52.8 in 2026 and 48.6 in 2025.

In a statement on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Vice-Chancellor Meenakshi Goyal said, “This improvement in Panjab University’s global standing reflects our continued commitment to strengthening interdisciplinary research and academic collaboration. It is the outcome of the collective efforts of our faculty, researchers, students, and staff. We will continue to build an enabling research ecosystem that encourages collaboration across disciplines, supports innovation, and addresses complex societal challenges aimed at Viksit Bharat through knowledge and research.”

The 2027 edition of the rankings, produced by Times Higher Education in association with Schmidt Science Fellows, assessed 1,058 institutions across 102 countries and territories, compared with 911 institutions in the 2026 edition. A total of 565 Asian institutions were ranked, up from 478 last year.

The Interdisciplinary Science Rankings assess universities’ contributions and commitment to research that brings together knowledge and methods from different academic disciplines to address complex challenges. The rankings cover collaborations involving multiple scientific disciplines as well as research combining scientific disciplines with areas such as the social sciences, education, psychology, law, economics, and clinical and health studies.

articles.title: U.S., Venezuela sign deal to re-establish military ties: Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Defence Secretary said that following the January capture of Nicolas Maduro by the U.S. military, the country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner”
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, speaking in Venezuela, said the two countries have signed an agreement to re-establish military ties, from training to intelligence sharing.

Mr. Hegseth said that following the January capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro by the U.S. military, the country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner.”
Mr. Hegseth also praised the “close cooperation” with interim President Delcy Rodriguez that allowed officials “to stabilise Venezuela and rid it of narco-terrorists once and for all.”
The Pentagon did not immediately offer further details on the new partnership.

Ms. Rodríguez separately lauded the opportunity to strengthen the military partnership. “I hope that this technical-military cooperation … can be brought to its highest possible level so that ... we may address common threats,” she said.
Mr. Hegseth’s visit underscores efforts by President Donald Trump’s administration to deepen its influence in the South American country since U.S. forces ousted Maduro in January.

Mr. Hegseth is the latest member of Mr. Trump’s Cabinet to travel to Venezuela following visits this year by the Interior and Energy secretaries, who have focused on efforts to tap its oil reserves and critical minerals. Mr. Trump said in August that Mr. Hegseth helped broker a sweeping deal for the U.S. to take control of some Venezuelan oil reserves.
The head of U.S. military operations in Latin America, Gen. Francis Donovan of U.S. Southern Command, also has met interim authorities in Venezuela at least twice this year.

The U.S. military has been expanding its attention on the region since Mr. Trump returned to the White House last year, with the Republican president promising to focus more on the Western Hemisphere and battle Latin American drug cartels.

To try to stem the flow of narcotics into the U.S. and the scourge of fatal overdoses, American forces have been attacking what the Trump administration says are boats smuggling drugs in the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean. At least 240 people have been killed since the administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” in September 2025, although U.S. officials have released little evidence publicly to support claims the vessels were carrying drugs.

articles.title: COVID-19 lessons should inform response to air pollution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Tackling air pollution already attracts considerable expenditure, but allocations do not consistently reflect the greatest health risks

There is an uncanny similarity between Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the virus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic, and air pollution. During the pandemic, the virus entered our bodies through the air we breathed; harmful particulate matter and toxic gases enter through the same respiratory route. Additionally, both damage multiple organs, including the lungs, heart and brain. Yet, while COVID-19 prompted an unprecedented emergency national response, air pollution continues to be treated largely as a seasonal inconvenience.

The harmful effects of air pollution are well-established. An adult takes approximately 20,000–25,000 breaths daily, meaning that even a relatively miniscule worsening of air quality can have substantial health consequences over time. This alone should make improving the quality of air an urgent public health priority.

articles.title: A regulatory fix for India’s campuses
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Ministry must act without delay and issue a statutory notification, consistent with the court’s judgment, for eligible educational campuses

India’s education infrastructure has always been the strongest foundation of its growth and development. However, recent Supreme Court judgments have reaffirmed that educational buildings exceeding 20,000 square metres require prior Environmental Clearance (EC) under the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006. Institutions that have already constructed such buildings without obtaining clearance are now left without any procedure to secure it, creating a serious obstacle. The issue has developed because of two major regulatory changes.

Before the EIA Notification, 2006, there was no built-up-area-based EC requirement for educational institutions. The Notification brought large construction projects, including educational campuses, within the prior EC framework. In December 2014, the Union government exempted schools, colleges and institutional hostels from EC, subject to environmental management conditions. The Kerala High Court quashed this exemption in March 2024. The government introduced a fresh exemption in January 2025, but Vanashakti challenged it before the Supreme Court. After staying its operation, the court cancelled the exemption in August 2025. Consequently, large educational buildings again became subject to prior EC requirements.
Science, Space & Environment Report: A regulatory fix for India’s campuses. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

• The Ministry must act without delay and issue a statutory notification, consistent with the court’s judgment, for eligible educational campuses
• India’s education infrastructure has always been the strongest foundation of its growth and development. However, recent Supreme Court judgments have reaffirmed that educational buildings exceeding 20,000 square metres require prior Environmental Clearance (EC) under the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006. Institutions that have already constructed such buildings without obtaining clearance are now left without any procedure to secure it, creating a serious obstacle. The issue has developed because of two major regulatory changes.
• Before the EIA Notification, 2006, there was no built-up-area-based EC requirement for educational institutions. The Notification brought large construction projects, including educational campuses, within the prior EC framework. In December 2014, the Union government exempted schools, colleges and institutional hostels from EC, subject to environmental management conditions. The Kerala High Court quashed this exemption in March 2024. The government introduced a fresh exemption in January 2025, but Vanashakti challenged it before the Supreme Court. After staying its operation, the court cancelled the exemption in August 2025. Consequently, large educational buildings again became subject to prior EC requirements.

articles.title: Police, magistrates, and sessions judges cannot refuse bail if offences are bailable: Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice N. Ramesh says they do not enjoy any discretion to deny bail in such cases and orders circulation of his verdict to all judicial officers in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry

Expressing shock over a case where a metropolitan magistrate and a sessions judge in Chennai had denied bail in a case booked for bailable offences, the Madras High Court has reminded judicial officers in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry that they do not enjoy any such discretion.

Justice N. Ramesh held that even if the accused had mentioned a wrong provision of the law under which they had sought bail, it would be the duty of the judicial officers to find out whether the offences for which the petitioners had been arrested were bailable or not, and then take an appropriate decision.

“If the offences are bailable and the accused is prepared to give bail, he shall be released under Section 478(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The police officer, the magistrate, the court of session, or this court would have no discretion to refuse,” the judge wrote.

The judge made it clear that the gravity of an accusation, the stage of investigation, an awaited forensic report, antecedents of the petitioner, or the apprehension of absconding or tampering with evidence could be cited as grounds only for denying bail in non-bailable offences and not in cases related to bailable offences.

Further, while granting bail for bailable offences, “the court may fix the amount of the bond and decide whether sureties are required. It may not attach any other condition. An accused who is indigent, or who is unable to give a bail bond within a week of his arrest, must be released on his own bond,” the judge added.

Justice Ramesh further made it clear that a bail granted in respect of bailable offences could be cancelled only by the High Court if the conduct of the accused, after his release, was found to be prejudicial to a fair trial. He also said that if a person had violated the conditions of a bail bond in some case, then he could be denied bail in the next case even if the offences in the subsequent case were bailable.

The judge pointed out that the BNSS, as well as special legislations related to criminal offences, clearly specify the list of offences, such as those which carry a maximum punishment of three years, which were bailable, and those which were non-bailable.

He directed the High Court’s Registrar General Deepthi Arivunithi to circulate a copy of his order to all Principal District and Sessions Judges and the Chief Judicial Magistrates in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry so that it could be brought to the notice of judicial officers across the State and the Union Territory. A copy should also be sent to the Director of the Tamil Nadu State Judicial Academy, the judge said.

The orders were passed while granting bail to P. Rajagopal of Thiruvanmiyur in Chennai, who was arrested by the Chennai Cyber Crime police on October 22, 2026, for having posted an obscene, abusive, and derogatory remark against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on the X handle of the accused on June 12, 2026.

The petitioner was booked under Sections 296(b) (using abusive words) of the BNSS and 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2000. However, there was nothing on record to show that the police had informed the accused that both the provisions were bailable, the judge said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

articles.title: BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi's U.S. remarks, says AI can predict his speeches
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP also said that Congress should consider sending an AI-generated version of its leader abroad because he keeps repeating the same words

The BJP on Thursday (November 19, 2026) slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for his remarks during his U.S. visit, accusing him of making “Hawai” allegations about India's electoral process and lowering the country's image on foreign soil.
The BJP also said that Congress should consider sending an AI-generated version of its leader abroad because he keeps repeating the same words.

Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Mr. Gandhi said Indian democracy is “sacred”, and the Congress is ready to face electoral defeats until people realise that the system has been “completely demolished”.
Mr. Gandhi also said that boycotting elections over alleged flaws in the system would bring an end to Indian democracy, which the Congress does not intend to do.

Addressing a press conference at the party headquarters, BJP spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi said it is unfortunate that Mr. Gandhi is making remarks against India in Chicago, the city where Swami Vivekananda had once brought glory to the country.
“Today, we have a leader of the opposition who is lowering the prestige of Mother India at the same place. This is unfortunate for the Congress and painful for Indians,” Mr. Trivedi said.
ALSO WATCH Watch: India facing ‘economic disaster’: Rahul Gandhi at Columbia university
He was responding to Mr. Gandhi's remarks questioning the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and concerns over electoral irregularities.

Referring to Mr. Gandhi's claim that a Brazilian model voted “23 times” in India, Mr. Trivedi questioned the basis of the charge. “Anyone coming from abroad should have an immigration record, shouldn't they? Just imagine, a leader of the opposition can make such ‘Hawai’ allegations,” he said.
Taking a swipe at Mr. Gandhi's frequent foreign visits, Mr. Trivedi said the Congress should stop spending money on sending him abroad.

articles.title: PM Modi pulls up India Inc over Make in India, employment, wages, quality, and lack of FTA planning
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While also highlighting the economic progress India has made over the course of his tenure as Prime Minister, Mr. Modi also pointed out several ways in which the private sector needed to improve

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (November 19, 2026) tore into gathered industry leaders on a variety of issues, including their lack of progress since the times of Mahatma Gandhi towards manufacturing in India, companies’ failures to increase employment and wages, the trend of exporters sending their highest quality items out of the country, and industry’s lack of preparedness to exploit benefits unleashed by Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).

While addressing the inaugural session of FICCI’s Annual General Meeting in Delhi, Mr. Modi also spoke about the various strengths of the economy, including its move from a ‘fragile five’ economy to the fastest-growing major economy in the world, the increase in per capita income, and the World Bank’s recognition of India’s poverty reduction efforts.
However, he also voiced several points of criticism against the Indian private sector. One of these had to do with the Make in India mission and the attempt to make India self reliant.
“In 1930, Gandhi came to you and said exactly this,” Mr. Modi said. “And even today, after all these years, I have to say the same thing. Is this your success or your failure?”

“Don’t take my word for it, at least listen to Gandhi,” he further exhorted the assembled industry leaders. “He too spoke of Swadeshi, he too spoke of a self-reliant India. And you have completed 100 years, yet things remain exactly where they were!”
India's growth story is creating new opportunities. Our industries must be ready to seize them. Speaking at FICCI's centenary convention. @ficci_india https://t.co/tJCw2NnpjW
The Prime Minister spoke about how this government has reduced corporate taxes to 22% and has ensured that individuals earning up to ₹12 lakh a year did not have to pay income tax.
However, he also castigated the assembled leaders for wanting even more, rather than passing on the benefits.
“Have you increased the salaries of your employees,” Mr. Modi asked. “Have you increased the number of your employees? No! ‘Modi ji, you do it, we’ll watch’. This is how it will continue.”

The Prime Minister also called on the private sector to improve the quality of products it sells in India, saying that the mindset where ‘export quality’ denotes high quality products needs to change.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 19 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 PM Modi pulls up India Inc over Make in India, employment, wages, quality, and lack of FTA planning

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

While also highlighting the economic progress India has made over the course of his tenure as Prime Minister, Mr. Modi also pointed out several ways in which the private sector needed to improve

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (November 19, 2026) tore into gathered industry leaders on a variety of issues, including their lack of progress since the times of Mahatma Gandhi towards manufacturing in India, companies’ failures to increase employment and wages, the trend of exporters sending their highest quality items out of the country, and industry’s lack of preparedness to exploit benefits unleashed by Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).

While addressing the inaugural session of FICCI’s Annual General Meeting in Delhi, Mr. Modi also spoke about the various strengths of the economy, including its move from a ‘fragile five’ economy to the fastest-growing major economy in the world, the increase in per capita income, and the World Bank’s recognition of India’s poverty reduction efforts.

However, he also voiced several points of criticism against the Indian private sector. One of these had to do with the Make in India mission and the attempt to make India self reliant.

“In 1930, Gandhi came to you and said exactly this,” Mr. Modi said. “And even today, after all these years, I have to say the same thing. Is this your success or your failure?”

“Don’t take my word for it, at least listen to Gandhi,” he further exhorted the assembled industry leaders. “He too spoke of Swadeshi, he too spoke of a self-reliant India. And you have completed 100 years, yet things remain exactly where they were!”

India's growth story is creating new opportunities. Our industries must be ready to seize them. Speaking at FICCI's centenary convention. @ficci_india https://t.co/tJCw2NnpjW

The Prime Minister spoke about how this government has reduced corporate taxes to 22% and has ensured that individuals earning up to ₹12 lakh a year did not have to pay income tax.

However, he also castigated the assembled leaders for wanting even more, rather than passing on the benefits.

“Have you increased the salaries of your employees,” Mr. Modi asked. “Have you increased the number of your employees? No! ‘Modi ji, you do it, we’ll watch’. This is how it will continue.”

The Prime Minister also called on the private sector to improve the quality of products it sells in India, saying that the mindset where ‘export quality’ denotes high quality products needs to change.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Prime Minister also called on the private sector to improve the quality of products it sells in India, saying that the mindset where ‘export quality’ denotes high quality products needs to change.

articles.title: Indian democracy 'sacred', boycotting polls will end it: Rahul Gandhi at University of Chicago
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished,” the Congress leader said

Indian democracy is "sacred" and the Congress is ready to face electoral defeats until people realise that the system has been completely demolished, Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said.

Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Mr. Gandhi said boycotting elections over alleged flaws in the electoral system would bring an end to Indian democracy, and the Congress party does not intend to do that.

"Indian democracy is sacred. For me to even say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200, 300 per cent proof," he said during the interaction moderated by Prof Robert Pape.
The Congress leader said asking the opposition to boycott elections would end democracy that very minute.

"But what happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't participate in the election?' If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that minute. And we don't want to end the structure of Indian democracy,” Mr. Gandhi said.
“So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished,” he said.

Mr. Gandhi was on a two-day visit to the U.S. during which he interacted with the students of Columbia University in New York on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and the University of Chicago on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).

articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi calls for continued dialogue with China to ease bilateral tensions
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Earlier in the day, Ms. Takaichi shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping and later held a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Thursday (November 19, 2026) called for continued dialogue and communication with China to ease bilateral tensions triggered by her remarks on Taiwan, saying Beijing is an "important neighbour" with which Tokyo has several outstanding issues.
Ms. Takaichi is in Shenzhen to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.

"China is an important neighbour, and between the two countries there are outstanding issues, and that is why it is important to continue communicating and having dialogue,” she told the media on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
Earlier in the day, Ms. Takaichi shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping and later held a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
When asked about her brief interaction with Mr. Xi, the Japanese PM said she thanked him for the invitation and congratulated him on successfully hosting the APEC summit.

Relations between Tokyo and Beijing have sharply deteriorated after Takaichi told parliament in November last year that a Chinese attack on Taiwan, a self-governed island claimed by China, could trigger a situation in which Japan's Self-Defence Forces might support US forces.
Her remarks infuriated China, prompting it to take a series of political and economic measures against Japan, including export restrictions on rare earths used in a wide range of high-tech products.
Asked about the controversy, Ms. Takaichi said Japan's four political documents governing its relations with China remained unchanged and continued to serve as the foundation of bilateral ties.

Tokyo will continue to advance a comprehensive strategic relationship of mutual benefit with Beijing while pursuing dialogue to protect their respective national interests and build constructive and stable ties, she said, according to the Hong Kong-based South China Morning Post.
Ms. Takaichi refrained from commenting on a hypothetical Taiwan contingency, saying Japan's position on Taiwan, as articulated in the 1972 Japan-China Joint Communique, remained unchanged.

articles.title: Yunus's ancestral home set ablaze as violence grips Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Crude bomb explosions rocked Bangladesh's capital before dawn, while former interim government chief Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home was torched in Chattogram. The unrest followed a Thursday (November 19, 2026) "lockdown" call by the banned Awami League, led by former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Police and witnesses said at least four people were wounded. Witnesses reported explosions of a series of improvised devices, arson attacks and vandalism in Dhaka despite stepped-up security.
Unidentified arsonists set fire to Mr. Yunus's paternal home at Chattogram's Panchlaish area after several branches of his Grameen Bank in different parts of Bangladesh were set on fire.

Newspaper reports said rival activists, presumably belonging to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), overnight attacked or set ablaze the residences of two Awami League leaders in Dhaka.

Police said they stepped up security overnight, mobilising more personnel at major flyovers across the capital. At the same time, officers were seen checking vehicles at entry and exit points and questioning motorcyclists and drivers of suspicious vehicles.

Awami League called the lockdown coinciding with the anniversary of a special tribunal verdict sentencing Ms. Hasina to death last year after trying her in absentia on charges of committing crimes against humanity.

Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest called the July Uprising that toppled her government. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India.

Officials said thousands of paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) troops were called out to maintain order in sensitive districts including southwestern Gopalganj district, Ms. Hasina's birthplace.

According to BDnews24 , police arrested 565 people in a 24-hour drive in Dhaka alone ahead of the lockdown, with one prominent person being former Education Minister in Ms. Hasina's cabinet Nurul Islam Nahid, who was detained from his Dhaka residence at midnight on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).

Prime Minister Tarique on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) night sought "democratic forces" unity to prevent "resurgence" of Awami League, describing it as a "terrorist outfit" and "fallen, defeated, and ousted fascist force" and called for actions for its "decisive defeat".

articles.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting LIVE: Xi-Trump-Putin summit begins in China; no peace ever forged by declining opportunities, says Trump
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: China-U.S. relations 'stable and improved', Xi says; Ukraine strikes Crimean bridge again as Trump says U.S., China want to help end war

Some in the West are comparing the three-way meeting to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the wartime leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union divided Germany and Berlin, carved out zones of influence in Europe, and agreed to establish the United Nations.
The Kremlin, which long has courted the concept of a “multipolar world” offering an equal say to all nations, plays down the Yalta comparisons, which are also unwelcome to China for similar reasons.

Fyodor Lukyanov, a pro-Kremlin foreign policy expert, noted that even as Moscow publicly rejects the Yalta analogy, it seems to believe the leaders could “reach agreements and make decisions that will determine global developments”.
Of the three nations, “it seems that only Russia really believes in the possibility of global control”, he told a recent roundtable.

Chatham House director Bronwen Maddox said in a commentary that “standing with Xi and Trump, Putin will look like one of the three main leaders of the world”, even though “Russia is no superpower” and its economy, overloaded with military spending, is dwindling.
She warned that “the danger for Ukraine is that Trump uses this summit to try to advance his notion of peace, including giving Russia territory it has not managed to seize by force”.

The meeting follows US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine held in Abu Dhabi last week for the first time in nine months. The negotiations produced few visible results as the parties stuck to their sharply divergent demands. -- AP

articles.title: U.S. court orders delivery of summonses to Doval, Goel through Delhi courts
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Citing the Hague Conventions and relevant provisions of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), a U.S. federal court Judge Katherine Polk Failla said foreign courts can serve summonses to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts

A U.S. federal court has ordered the delivery of summonses to National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Goel through Delhi courts in connection with a lawsuit filed by Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.
Mr. Pannun is wanted by Indian probe agencies on various terror charges.

In an order dated November 13, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York directed its clerk to send the summonses and accompanying judicial documents to the Patiala House District Court for Mr. Doval, and the Dwarka and Tis Hazari district courts for Mr. Goel.

"The court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court," says an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla.
Citing the Hague Conventions and relevant provisions of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), Ms. Failla said foreign courts can serve summonses to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts.
The CPC permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts notified by the central government to be transmitted to Indian courts and served in the same manner as summonses issued by domestic courts.
The U.S. court order stated that the standard procedure for serving the summonses through India's central authority under the Hague Convention had been attempted but rejected.
The court subsequently authorised an alternative mode of service under Article 19 of the convention and the relevant provisions of India's CPC.
Mr. Pannun, a U.S.-based legal counsel for the banned organisation Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), has filed the civil lawsuit seeking damages over an alleged attempt on his life.
He has accused Mr. Doval of orchestrating the alleged assassination plot with the involvement of India's external intelligence agency RAW.

articles.title: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.

The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.

GTA 6 is now live on Blinkit! 🎮 It took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released. In the meantime, we built Blinkit so that you can get the game delivered in minutes. We've launched it in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata & Ahmedabad (launching in more cities between today and tomorrow). We'll deliver a physical box with a download code inside (the box is a nice collectible for your shelf). Get yours now and start downloading so you're ready to play from 19th November. Expecting a suspicious number of sick leaves over the next few days 😮‍💨

In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.

For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.

Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.

Grand Theft Auto V arrived in India in September 2013, priced at around ₹3,000 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. But its second life here began after PUBG Mobile was banned in September 2020. Several of India’s biggest streamers, including Dynamo and MortaL, turned to other games, GTA V among them, and roleplay helped make it a mainstay of Indian livestreaming.

A roleplay server is a fan-run version of GTA V’s online world where players invent characters with names, jobs and backstories, from cab drivers and paramedics to cops and small-time crooks, and inhabit them for hours. Soulcity, launched by S8UL and Velocity Gaming in early 2023, became one of India’s biggest GTA V roleplay servers and helped create a new breed of gaming star. S8UL co-founder Lokesh Jain, better known as 8Bit Goldy, played a character called Rocket Singh on the server. The scene grew big enough for S8UL to sign creators such as Sunny Jha, aka Pitaji Playz, specifically for its GTA roleplay roster.

articles.title: IIIT-H students develop web plugin to translate text into Indian Sign Language
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The tool is a simple plugin that lets you select text on a web page, producing a 3D avatar that signs in the Indian Sign Language

The Indian Sign Language (ISL) uses gestures to represent complex words and sentences and has its own grammar and word order. People with hearing impairments find it a challenge to read content online. To address this gap, Masthan Sharif Shaik and Mohammed Raza, third-year BTech. students from the Center for Visual Information Technology (CVIT), IIIT-Hyderabad, under the supervision of Prof. C.V. Jawahar and Prof. Vinay Namboodiri (University of Bath, U.K.), developed a cost-effective plugin that can be added to any website.

The plugin can run inside a browser in real time, without any real hardware or an AI model running on a server. “Websites today support captions, screen readers, and high-contrast modes, but almost none of them can show content in sign language. Existing signing avatars are either costly motion-capture systems, heavy AI models that need powerful GPUs, or systems built from sign notation – all of which require linguistic experts and also tend to move robotically,” Sharif said.

The researchers first took the official Indian Sign Language Research And Training Centre’s sign-language dictionary videos and used computer vision to recover each signer’s 3D body, hand and finger movements. “Automatic reconstruction, however, often gets fingers wrong, and in sign language a wrong finger can change the meaning. So, we built an annotation tool, Gizmo, to correct only the few key poses of each sign instead of every frame,” Sharif said.

There is an offline preprocessing that takes place where sentences are converted into ISL word order. For example, a sentence such as “He will come home” in ISL becomes “He home come”. When a sentence like the former is highlighted and the ‘Click To Sign’ button is selected, the stored motion for each sign is fetched, and the signs are blended smoothly, allowing the avatar to sign the whole sentence fluidly. Words without a sign are fingerspelled letter by letter.

The movements are more natural in this case because the avatar replays motion captured from real signers rather than motion generated from notation. Additionally, what makes this task unique is that it all happens without a GPU. “The heavy computer-vision work happens once, offline, when the sign dictionary is built. Viewing a sentence only replays and blends stored motion together, which an ordinary laptop handles”, says Sharif.

When tested on deaf and hard-of-hearing signers, the ISL signers understood about 89% of sentences signed by the avatar. However, the lack of facial features in the avatar was cited as a drawback because expressions typically include grammar in ISL, as well as signs that change form in context. “We will work to incorporate this in our next iteration,” says Sharif.

“Indian Sign language (ISL) seriously lacks resources and technologies”, explains Prof. Jawahar. The group is working in two directions – Sign Language Synthesis as well as Sign Language Understanding. The plugin is related to sign language synthesis from text on low cost commodity hardware.

articles.title: GTA VI: Gamers enter Vice City as most-awaited game is rolled out globally
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Game unlocked at midnight on November 19 in each market; Rockstar says story follows criminal couple Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval in Vice City
The wait is over. ‌After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, the most anticipated video game release in history is finally ​here.

“Grand Theft Auto VI” became available as midnight struck in New Zealand on Thursday (November 19, 2026), with the launch then following the clock around ⁠the world. Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles in anticipation.

The release, with events worldwide and many users taking days off work to play, marks the latest instalment in one of entertainment’s most successful franchises. Since its 1997 debut, “Grand Theft Auto” has become one of the best-selling video game series of all time.

“I’ve been waiting 13 years to ‌play,” said 20-year-old Jonah Bowen-Brown from Australia’s southern island of Tasmania, who persuaded his mother to give him and his brother a week off work at the family-run fragrance shop, Whiff-it!.
“She was really against it at first,” said Bowen-Brown. “I had to say, mum, please, please, I need ‌it.”
A gamer plays Grand Theft Auto VI in Miami, Florida | Photo Credit: Reuters
The game is made by Take-Two Interactive’s Rockstar Games and available on Sony’s PlayStation 5 and Microsoft’s Xbox Series X and S consoles.

The original “Grand Theft ‌Auto” ⁠looks basic by today’s standards, and its missions — stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates — angered politicians and parents. But it delighted ⁠gamers.

Each successive release delivered more sophisticated graphics and storytelling. “Grand Theft Auto V”, released in 2013 and set in the fictional Los Santos, a stand-in for Los Angeles, became one of the best-selling video games ever.
While retaining the series’ trademark mix of crime, driving and morally dubious missions, it added activities ranging from parachute jumps to cinema visits and radio stations satirising US culture.

articles.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Over one lakh evacuated in Odisha as landfall likely near Gopalpur; red alert for three A.P. districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The IMD says the corridor for landfall, likely on Nov. 20 noon, stretches from Andhra's Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh to Odisha's Puri

The Odisha government has set up 9,299 shelters, evacuated over one lakh people to safety, deployed 305 emergency response teams and closed educational institutes in several districts as it has stepped up precautionary measures in view of Cyclone ‘Akvan’, which is likely to cross between Gopalpur and Puri on Friday (November 20, 2026), Chief Secretary Anu Garg said.
The State government is making all-encompassing preparations to tackle the cyclone’s impact, with priority being given to ensure “zero casualties”, she said.
As a precautionary measure, the chief secretary said, “Altogether 1,05,304 people have so far been evacuated, and this process is going on. They have been moved to 1,224 cyclone and flood shelters.”
Altogether 45,364 people have been evacuated in Ganjam, and 18,000 in Gajapati, she said.
Severe cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ continues to move northwards with a speed of 17 kmph, the IMD said in its latest update on Thursday afternoon (November 19, 2026).

It is likely to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by noon of 20th November, 2026 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph, it added.

The Srikakulam and Vizianagaram district administrations are on high alert ahead of Cyclone Akvan, which is expected to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday (November 20, 2026). articles.title: Yadgir ZP CEO directs officials to ensure effective implementation of schemes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Newly appointed Chief Executive Officer Jubin Mohapatra chairs his maiden meeting with district-level officers of various departments

Chairing a maiden meeting with the district level officers of various government departments, the newly appointed Chief Executive Officer of the Yadgir Zilla Panchayat Jubin Mohapatra has directed them to take concrete steps for the effective implementation of departmental schemes and ensure that funds are utilised within the stipulated timeframe without allowing them to lapse.
Mr. Mohapatra, who assumed charge as the CEO on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), chaired a review meeting in Zilla Panchayat’s VC Hall on Wednesday (November 18).
He stressed the need for timely and target-oriented expenditure of grants released under various Zilla Panchayat heads and other State government programmes.

Emphasising the effective rollout of the State government’s five guarantee schemes apart from the sixth ‘Bhoo Guarantee’ initiative, the CEO instructed officials to ensure that the benefits of every beneficiary-oriented scheme reach eligible people without delay.
He cautioned officers against any irregularities and directed them to discharge their duties responsibly in strict adherence to government guidelines and directives.

Calling for close inter-departmental coordination, Mr. Mohapatra asked officials to keep updated progress reports of all schemes ready at all times and bring any operational issues to his immediate notice.

Announcing a citizen-centric measure, the CEO said a dedicated public grievance redressal cell would soon be opened at the Zilla Panchayat office to address public issues promptly. He urged officials to focus on resolving grievances in a fair and lawful manner.
In-charge Deputy Secretary of the Zilla Panchayat Sharanabasav and various district-level officers attended the meeting.

fullParagraphs: The Villupuram All Women Police on Thursday (November 19, 2026) arrested the headmaster of a government primary school at Arungurukkai Pudur near Thiruvennainallur, under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, on charges of sexually harassing girl students.

According to the police, the headmaster Vikraman had sexually harassed a few girl students of Class V. The children reported the incident to their parents, following which a team of officials from the School Education Department, led by Block Education Officer Ambika, visited the school and spoke to the students.
The BEO submitted a report, after which the District Elementary Education Officer Ilamathi ordered the suspension of Vikraman. He was subsequently arrested and remanded to custody.

fullParagraphs: Private BS-VI vehicles older than 10 years must have their Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates renewed every six months

The government has revised the validity periods of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates, allowing newer BS-VI-compliant vehicles to go longer between renewals while retaining shorter validity periods for older vehicles.

articles.title: Unions oppose privatisation of Visakhapatnam Port Hospital, plan protest on November 20
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime land worth around ₹350 crore is being offered to a private firm for ₹9 crore, the unions allege
All-party trade unions representing workers at the Visakhapatnam Port have strongly opposed the port management’s proposal to privatise the Visakhapatnam Port Hospital.

Demanding the immediate withdrawal of the move and the cancellation of tenders scheduled to be opened on November 21, the unions announced a one-hour protest at the start of duty hours on Friday (November 20, 2026).

Addressing a press conference at the Jagadamba office in Visakhapatnam on Thursday, leaders of the Port All-Party Trade Unions termed the decision to hand over the hospital to private entities an “extremely irresponsible act” that jeopardises the healthcare security of nearly 40,000 port workers, employees, pensioners and their family members.

The union leaders questioned the rationale behind privatising the facility when the Visakhapatnam Port possesses assets worth thousands of crores of rupees, valuable land, its own buildings and substantial reserve funds, while generating annual profits running into hundreds of crores. Calling it shameful for a profit-making port authority to claim it cannot independently upgrade its own hospital, they demanded that the management clarify its intentions to the public.

Raising serious allegations over the terms of the proposal, the unions expressed concern that prime land abutting the National Highway—estimated to be worth around ₹350 crore—is being proposed for handover to a private firm for a mere ₹9 crore. They questioned why the port, despite earning hundreds of crores in annual revenue, could not spend roughly ₹50 crore of its own funds to equip the hospital with modern medical facilities.

Warning that private operators work for profit rather than public service, the leaders said that privatisation would make medical care expensive and impose a severe financial burden on serving employees, retired staff and their dependents. Sacrificing the healthcare security of more than 40,000 dependent families for the commercial interests of private firms was unacceptable, they added.

Instead of pursuing privatisation, the unions demanded that the port management fulfil its social responsibility by upgrading the facility into a full-fledged super-speciality hospital using its own funds, recruiting specialist doctors and medical staff, and procuring state-of-the-art medical equipment and technology.

Veera Raghavulu, and VPDMS (BMS) leader K.S.V.G.K. Patnaik were present.

articles.title: OMCs achieve 0.08% biodiesel blending in H1, lower than target; cite feedstock shortage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: In the fiscal year 2025-26, OMCs had achieved an overall biodiesel blending of 0.18%

India’s three state-owned oil marketing companies (OMCs) – Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and Bharat Petroleum Corporation – achieved an overall biodiesel blending of just 0.08% in the first half of FY27, “significantly below” the indicative target of 5% by 2030, citing limited feedstock availability.
Biodiesel is produced from various feedstocks, including non-edible vegetable oils, animal fat and recycled cooking oil.

Between April and September 2026, the three OMCs sold approximately 4,900 crore litres of diesel. Of this, more than 4,700 crore litres were sold without any biodiesel blending. The remaining 200 crore litres comprised diesel blended with approximately four crore litres of biodiesel, translating into an average blending rate of 2% in the blended portion, they said in a joint statement.
Consequently, biodiesel accounted for 0.08% of the total diesel sold by the OMCs during the six-month period.
The performance also marks a decline from FY26, when the three companies achieved an overall biodiesel blending rate of 0.18%.

The OMCs reiterated that biodiesel-blended diesel conforms to Bureau of Indian Standards specification BIS 1460, which prescribes requirements for automotive diesel fuel, and is covered under the publicly notified National Policy on Biofuels.

They also pointed out that biodiesel blending is an established global practice, with countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia and Brazil adopting blending levels ranging from 10% to 50%, depending on feedstock availability.

articles.title: Israel army says it completed ground operation in central Gaza
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area
Israel's military said that a ground operation involving tanks in central Gaza that began the previous day despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire had come to an end on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The Defence Ministry's body in charge of civilian affairs in Palestinian territories, Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT), said in a statement that Palestinians would again be free to move in the targeted areas near the Al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps.

"We would like to inform you that the activity has ended, and the Salah al-Din axis has been reopened," COGAT said in an Arabic-language statement on Facebook, referring to the war-shattered territory's main thoroughfare.

On Wednesday (November 18, 2026), the Israeli military said it had launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, beyond the so-called "Yellow Line" which separates areas under Israeli military and Hamas control following an October 2025 ceasefire.
An AFP journalist reported seeing Israeli tanks positioning themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp.
Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area.
The military said in a statement that the operation had been launched to "dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".

A Gaza security source told AFP there had been "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday".
Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal that came after two years of devastating war sparked by Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza Health Ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

articles.title: COP31 negotiators publish revised deal draft with no mention of fossil fuels
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on November 16

The latest iteration of the COP 31 draft cover text has eliminated references to fossil fuel phase-out and net-zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries. This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus.

The COP31 Presidency’s revised draft cover decision, dated November 19, has 80 paragraphs, down from 144 in the November 16 version. The summit officially ends on November 20, though negotiations frequently overshoot into the weekend.

A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated.

However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, scaling up the use of carbon capture utilisation technologies and making early warning systems universal by 2027, continue to find mention in the text. A broad commitment to triple adaptation finance also remains.

“ The draft cover text weaves the 35% electricity in final energy consumption by 2035, alongside tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling the rate of energy efficiency improvement by 2030, ” Ajay Mathur, India’s lead negotiator at Paris COP and former DG, International Solar Alliance, said in a statement. The electricity use in India went up by 13% in 2025 due to the Hormuz crisis alone. It will be an ambitious goal for India to achieve 35% electrification by 2035, but due to the increasing amount of renewable energy in the Indian energy mix, we will be near the 32-34% mark by 2035. ”

“We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS) in a statement. “Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

articles.title: Third Ukrainian strike in 4 days halts rail traffic on Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort

A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Russian-held Crimea halted rail traffic across the span, officials said Thursday (November 19, 2026), after earlier strikes shut down the road section of the landmark that is a symbol of Moscow's invasion.
Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, but it resumed in the afternoon, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti .

The Ukrainian strikes seemed calculated to embarrass Russian President Vladimir Putin as he met in China with President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, as well as to demonstrate that Kyiv still holds cards in the war and to undermine Russia's argument that its victory is inevitable.

The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort and fear being sidelined by Mr. Trump's direct talks with Mr. Putin.
“We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that,” Mr. Putin told reporters in Shenzhen, China.
He insisted the bridge is a civilian asset, adding that he had ordered the bridge closed to the transport of military hardware or ammunition.
Mr. Putin also said that the road side of the bridge had been “seriously damaged” but vowed to rebuild it.
The rail section is believed to be stronger than the road side, to bear the greater weight of cargo wagons.

The 19-kilometre (12-mile) Kerch Bridge is a key route for military and civilian supplies to Crimea, which Moscow seized in defiance of international law in 2014 and uses to support front-line troops. It is a potent reminder of Russia's illegal annexation of the territory and has been a prime target for Ukraine.

A large section of the road deck and an arch collapsed in the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, according to Mr. Zelenskyy, and the train track was damaged by domestically produced Neptune missiles, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said.

articles.title: Riyadh's tallest building damaged as Saudi reports new Houthi attacks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Iran-backed Houthis have stepped up their attacks against Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, striking targets including airports, energy infrastructure, military sites and Riyadh's financial district

A skyscraper in Riyadh housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund was damaged on Thursday (November 19, 2026), witnesses told AFP , as the kingdom reported new attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
In the early hours of Thursday (November 19, 2026), AFP journalists in the Saudi capital reported a powerful blast was heard.
Around the same time, civil defence authorities issued a warning for "potential danger" but said minutes later that the danger had passed.
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it had "addressed a missile threat launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh".
"Initial assessment indicates the impact of debris, with material damage currently being surveyed," said coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki.
Witnesses later told AFP that Riyadh's Public Investment Fund Tower, which at 80 storeys is the tallest in the city, had been damaged.
"The facade is damaged across several floors, with windows blown out," said one person who requested anonymity.
"The damage also affected some of the buildings surrounding PIF tower, causing the glass facades on some to shatter. Some of the buildings are residential," the witness added.
Two other witnesses confirmed the damage to the tower, which AFP was unable to visit.

articles.title: Why data interoperability is critical to the future of hospital care
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The future of critical care will be defined by how effectively the information is connected, interpreted and applied

In an intensive care unit, every second matters. A critically ill patient may be connected to several devices, including patient monitors, ventilators and infusion pumps, while laboratory systems and electronic health records continuously generate additional information. Together, these systems create a large and rapidly-changing picture of the patient’s condition. However, when the information remains fragmented across devices and platforms, clinicians may spend valuable time locating, verifying and reconciling data before they can act.

This makes interoperability a clinical priority in critical care, not simply an information technology requirement. Integration enables systems to exchange data, but true interoperability ensures that the information being exchanged is accurate, interpretable and clinically relevant. This can help care teams coordinate and prioritise interventions more effectively while reducing the need to move between multiple systems to assemble a clinical picture.

The future of critical care will be defined by how effectively the information is connected, interpreted and applied

In an intensive care unit, every second matters. A critically ill patient may be connected to several devices, including patient monitors, ventilators and infusion pumps, while laboratory systems and electronic health records continuously generate additional information. Together, these systems create a large and rapidly-changing picture of the patient’s condition. However, when the information remains fragmented across devices and platforms, clinicians may spend valuable time locating, verifying and reconciling data before they can act.

This makes interoperability a clinical priority in critical care, not simply an information technology requirement. Integration enables systems to exchange data, but true interoperability ensures that the information being exchanged is accurate, interpretable and clinically relevant. This can help care teams coordinate and prioritise interventions more effectively while reducing the need to move between multiple systems to assemble a clinical picture.

articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia

The story so far: The battle for the most sought after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer after the U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule (IFR) barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia. The new, yet to be published, rule also restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government.

China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”
The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit.

The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but a legal tool to control the flow took shape only during the first Trump term when the administration passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018.

It gave the U.S. a legal weapon to control the movement of advanced technology originating from the country. Its primary purpose was to curb export of top-tier chips that had dual-use — both commercial and military purposes — to countries like China, Russia and Iran.

articles.title: Hyderabad doctor brings down rare disease drug cost from ₹9 crore to ₹2.5 lakh; seven children to get free treatment
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30; the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year

Imagine having a medicine that could help manage your child’s rare genetic condition, but being unable to afford it because a year’s treatment costs as much as ₹9 crore. For seven families in India, that situation could soon change.

Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30, following an initiative led by Hyderabad-based paediatrician Dr. Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India.

The development is significant not just because the families will receive the medicine without paying for it, but also because its cost has been brought down through pharmaceutical compounding in the Netherlands. While the commercial version of the drug costs approximately ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child annually, the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year.

The medicine has been prepared by Transvaal Pharmacy in The Hague, Netherlands, with support from the Netherlands-based Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF). The first batch will be handed over to the parents of the seven children along with the necessary documentation and individual import permissions. The families have secured approvals for one year of treatment. As the compounded medicine has a shelf life of six months, it will be imported in two batches.

The initiative began after Arav, a child under the care of Dr. Sivaranjani, was diagnosed with AHDS, also known as MCT8 deficiency. The condition is caused by mutations affecting the MCT8 gene, which plays an important role in transporting thyroid hormones into brain cells. Tiratricol, also known as TRIAC, acts on thyroid hormone receptors and may help overcome some effects of the deficiency. It also helps minimise complications associated with peripheral thyrotoxicosis.

Although the medicine was available in Europe, its commercial price put it beyond the reach of most Indian families. Arav’s mother, Pavitra Sirolkar, had to arrange approximately ₹12 lakh to ₹13 lakh for just one month’s supply of the medicine from Germany. Dr. Sivaranjani initially approached paediatricians, endocrinologists and paediatric neurologists to explore ways of procuring the drug. Doctors at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, where five other children with the same condition had been identified, were also approached.

Attempts to obtain the medicine through pharmaceutical company Egetis Therapeutics and its compassionate-use programme did not succeed. The situation eventually prompted Dr. Sivaranjani to take the issue to social media. On September 7, she posted an appeal seeking help for the family and urged people to tag the Prime Minister, Union Health Minister and other government representatives. The appeal gained attention, bringing it to the notice of PAF.

The foundation subsequently explored the possibility of preparing the medicine through pharmaceutical compounding using the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Transvaal Pharmacy conducted test batches and developed a formulation for the seven children. The initial group included Arav and five children receiving treatment at CMC Vellore. A seventh child, aged one year, was identified after his father contacted Dr Sivaranjani following her social media appeal.

According to PAF, the total cost of providing one year’s treatment to all seven children is €14,200, approximately ₹15.08 lakh. Of this, Dr Sivaranjani raised approximately ₹6.09 lakh in India, while PAF undertook to raise the remaining €8,600, approximately ₹9.13 lakh, in the Netherlands. The medicine will be provided to all seven families free of cost.

While the November 30 handover addresses the immediate treatment requirements of the seven children, Dr. Sivaranjani believes that importing the medicine cannot be a permanent solution. She plans to approach the Union government and work with Access to Medicines India and other organisations to explore the possibility of getting the medicine compounded in India and making it accessible to more children.

The medicine has been prepared by Transvaal Pharmacy in The Hague, Netherlands, with support from the Netherlands-based Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF). The first batch will be handed over to the parents of the seven children along with the necessary documentation and individual import permissions. The families have secured approvals for one year of treatment. As the compounded medicine has a shelf life of six months, it will be imported in two batches.

The initiative began after Arav, a child under the care of Dr. Sivaranjani, was diagnosed with AHDS, also known as MCT8 deficiency. The condition is caused by mutations affecting the MCT8 gene, which plays an important role in transporting thyroid hormones into brain cells. Tiratricol, also known as TRIAC, acts on thyroid hormone receptors and may help overcome some effects of the deficiency. It also helps minimise complications associated with peripheral thyrotoxicosis.

Although the medicine was available in Europe, its commercial price put it beyond the reach of most Indian families. Arav’s mother, Pavitra Sirolkar, had to arrange approximately ₹12 lakh to ₹13 lakh for just one month’s supply of the medicine from Germany. Dr. Sivaranjani initially approached paediatricians, endocrinologists and paediatric neurologists to explore ways of procuring the drug. Doctors at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, where five other children with the same condition had been identified, were also approached.

Attempts to obtain the medicine through pharmaceutical company Egetis Therapeutics and its compassionate-use programme did not succeed. The situation eventually prompted Dr. Sivaranjani to take the issue to social media. On September 7, she posted an appeal seeking help for the family and urged people to tag the Prime Minister, Union Health Minister and other government representatives. The appeal gained attention, bringing it to the notice of PAF.

The foundation subsequently explored the possibility of preparing the medicine through pharmaceutical compounding using the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Transvaal Pharmacy conducted test batches and developed a formulation for the seven children. The initial group included Arav and five children receiving treatment at CMC Vellore. A seventh child, aged one year, was identified after his father contacted Dr Sivaranjani following her social media appeal.

According to PAF, the total cost of providing one year’s treatment to all seven children is €14,200, approximately ₹15.08 lakh. Of this, Dr Sivaranjani raised approximately ₹6.09 lakh in India, while PAF undertook to raise the remaining €8,600, approximately ₹9.13 lakh, in the Netherlands. The medicine will be provided to all seven families free of cost.

While the November 30 handover addresses the immediate treatment requirements of the seven children, Dr. Sivaranjani believes that importing the medicine cannot be a permanent solution. She plans to approach the Union government and work with Access to Medicines India and other organisations to explore the possibility of getting the medicine compounded in India and making it accessible to more children.
