articles.title: GTA VI generates record $1.1 billion pre-order revenue
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year

As Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI officially launches today , November 19, 2026, a market intelligence report from Sensor Tower highlights an unprecedented shift in consumer engagement and industry revenue.

According to Sensor Tower’s report, the title generated $1.1 billion in pre-order revenue globally across PlayStation and Xbox consoles prior to release, with 11.3 million copies sold. This accomplishment marks the largest pre-launch revenue total on record.

The analytics firms project that total sales could reach $3.2 billion by the end of 2026. Beyond financial performance, the report forecasts a noticeable reallocation of consumer attention across the broader digital landscape.
Daily active user metrics across competing games and entertainment platforms are expected to see a measurable decline as players engage with the new release.
Sensor Tower estimates the average GTA VI player age at approximately 34 years old. This audience displays high companion engagement on second-screen platforms, including Discord, TikTok, and Twitch.
With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year.

articles.title: The average cost of a thali has jumped by 16% in less than 10 months
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Food inflation has raised meal costs, forcing households to spend a larger share of their wages on food
Food inflation in India steeply climbed to 8.9% last month, which is the highest inflation recorded in at least 22 months of the new series and the highest this year.

The prices of several food items have surged by a large margin between January and October this year. For instance, the price of one kilogram of onions increased by over 100% since March this year. Essential commodities like garlic (22%) and rice (11%) also saw a sharp surge in their retail prices.

Macroeconomic & Financial Update: The average cost of a thali has jumped by 16% in less than 10 months. This development reflects key trends in India's fiscal roadmap, monetary policy transmission, and banking sector resilience.

articles.title: India’s health services has banned reuse of single-use medical devices. But who decides what’s safe?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Unsafe reuse can harm patients, and billing for a reused device as if it were new is indefensible. But there is a bigger question that needs answering: who decides whether a device can be safely reprocessed, and on what evidence?

I was at Asan Medical Center in Seoul, watching liver transplants at one of the best programmes in the world, just as my own transplant career was beginning. The surgeon fired an expensive surgical stapler, finished the job and threw the device away. I was astonished.

Back home in India, we often used the same stapler again and again, until we felt it was no longer safe. It was so expensive that our patients could afford it only if the cost was shared among many of them.

That memory came back when the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) issued its directive of October 16, 2026 that bans the reuse of devices labelled for single use in all public and private healthcare facilities. The concerns it cites include the risk of infection, possible breaches of existing laws, and cases where patients or government schemes were reportedly charged the full price for reused devices.

These are fair concerns. Unsafe reuse can harm patients, and billing for a reused device as if it were new is indefensible. But there is a bigger question: who decides whether a device can be safely reprocessed, and on what evidence?

Think about rockets. For decades, they were thrown away after a single flight. Then Elon Musk’s SpaceX built boosters that could land, be checked and fly again, and spaceflight became much cheaper. If rockets can be reused, why not medical devices?

In two 2018 Heart Asia editorials, Thomas Crawford, Kim Eagle and colleagues point out that the single-use label is usually decided by the manufacturer, not by an independent regulator who has checked whether it could be safely reused.

A manufacturer that sells a single-use device earns money from every new purchase. Testing a device for reuse is expensive, and the single-use label avoids that cost. Every device thrown away is also a new sale. That said, manufacturers often have good reasons to limit use. Many devices have narrow tubes, fine hinges and delicate coatings that are hard to clean and check properly.

The truth about device reuse in India is not flattering. For years, hospitals have reprocessed devices without consistent protocols, proper tracking or any systematic record of outcomes. Our record on pricing is just as troubling. In 2017, Maharashtra’s Food and Drug Administration reportedly investigated eight private hospitals over the reuse of 1,306 catheters across more than 1,000 patients. Reports also said patients were charged a large part of the maximum retail price for reused balloon catheters.

Reprocessing is more than sterilising. A device can be sterile and still be weakened, unreliable or contaminated in ways the cleaning method does not reach. Depending on the device and the rules that apply to it, a reprocessor has to show that cleaning and sterilisation work, that the device still performs as it should, and that the whole process meets quality and reporting standards.

In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration treats anyone who reprocesses a single-use device as a manufacturer, with the same regulatory duties. Canada, Japan and the European Union have also set up rules for reprocessing, although the details differ from country to country.

articles.title: Elusive peace: On Kashmir terror attack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Restoration of Statehood is essential for peace in Jammu and Kashmir

Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.
Editorial Context: Elusive peace: On Kashmir terror attack. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Restoration of Statehood is essential for peace in Jammu and Kashmir

Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.

articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: Construction activities on Kaziranga wildlife corridors flagged
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: An Eastern Assam-based environment activist writes to the Supreme Court-constituted Central Empowered Committee, highlighting the concerns

An eastern Assam-based environmental activist has reminded the Supreme Court–constituted Central Empowered Committee (CEC) to continue construction activities on the wildlife corridors of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve.

Kaziranga has nine notified wildlife corridors and several dandis or animal pathways. Animals use these corridors and dandis mostly to escape to the hills of Karbi Anglong district when the park is flooded during the monsoon months.

In a letter to the CEC’s Member-Secretary on November 16, Rohit Choudhury said he had brought such construction activities to the notice of the Committee on May 11. He lamented the lack of action against these activities, violating the Supreme Court’s April 2019 order.

“We order that all kinds of mining and related activities along the aforesaid Kaziranga National Park area and in the entire catchment area of rivers, streams and rivulets originating in the Karbi Anglong Hill ranges and flowing into Kaziranga National Park, including the Tiger Reserve, are restrained. No new construction shall be permitted on private lands which form part of the nine identified animal corridors,” the apex court’s order read.

“Despite this clear and categorical prohibition, the Government of Assam has displayed a disturbing disregard for the mandate of the Supreme Court by permitting and facilitating unlawful construction activities within these ecologically sensitive wildlife corridors,” Mr. Choudhury wrote.

He reminded the CEC of photographic evidence of a building under construction on the Haldhibari Wildlife Corridor attached to his May 11 letter. “The construction activity was allowed to proceed unabated and has now reached an advanced stage of completion,” he wrote, attaching recent photographs of the construction site.

Mr. Choudhury said the CEC’s inability to take up the matter six months ago “effectively afforded the concerned authorities sufficient time to continue and substantially complete the illegal construction”.
He said such delays in addressing matters of grave environmental significance seriously undermine the purpose and efficacy of the CEC’s mandate.
The activist further said the CEC did not inform the Supreme Court of any violation of its April 12, 2019, order for necessary action.

“This persistent failure of enforcement has emboldened continued violations and weakened the protection envisaged by the Supreme Court,” he said, urging the CEC to recommend contempt proceedings against the officials responsible for permitting, facilitating or failing to prevent these blatant violations of the court’s binding directions.

articles.title: Kedarnath generates 73 tonnes of waste during 2026 Char Dham Yatra
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 65.65 lakh pilgrims visit four Char Dham shrines and Hemkund Sahib in 2026 as Badrinath portals close for winter

Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year.
According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard.
Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025.
The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added.

To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. The drive mobilised over 6,000 pilgrims to carry 14 tonnes of waste down to a collection point, from where it was sent for segregation and disposal.”

The increase in waste generation comes amid a broader rise in pilgrim numbers across Uttarakhand’s Char Dham circuit, according to a comparative analysis released by the Dehradun-based SDC Foundation.

Prepared by Anoop Nautiyal and Praveen Upreti, the study found that 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the four Char Dham shrines — Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri — and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, registering a 29% increase over 51.07 lakh in 2025. The pilgrimage season extended from mid-April to mid-November.

Kedarnath recorded 19,33,138 pilgrims, a 9% rise over the previous year. However, its average daily footfall declined by around 6%, from 10,113 pilgrims in 2025 to 9,476 in 2026. The foundation attributed the higher cumulative numbers partly to a longer pilgrimage season and fewer weather-related disruptions. Kedarnath remained operational for 204 days, compared with 175 days last year.

The SDC Foundation report also flagged concerns over pilgrim safety, recording 297 fatalities across the five shrines in 2026, compared with 182 in 2025. Health-related natural deaths alone increased by 81%, from 159 to 288, with Kedarnath accounting for 142 such deaths.

Vehicle movement during the Char Dham Yatra also witnessed a significant rise, increasing from 5,14,016 in 2025 to 6,68,877 in 2026 (till November 14). This represents an increase of 1,54,861 vehicles, or more than 30% over the previous year.

Around 65.65 lakh pilgrims visit four Char Dham shrines and Hemkund Sahib in 2026 as Badrinath portals close for winter

Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year.

According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard.

Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025.

The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added.

To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. The drive mobilised over 6,000 pilgrims to carry 14 tonnes of waste down to a collection point, from where it was sent for segregation and disposal.”

The increase in waste generation comes amid a broader rise in pilgrim numbers across Uttarakhand’s Char Dham circuit, according to a comparative analysis released by the Dehradun-based SDC Foundation.

Prepared by Anoop Nautiyal and Praveen Upreti, the study found that 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the four Char Dham shrines — Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri — and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, registering a 29% increase over 51.07 lakh in 2025. The pilgrimage season extended from mid-April to mid-November.

Kedarnath recorded 19,33,138 pilgrims, a 9% rise over the previous year. However, its average daily footfall declined by around 6%, from 10,113 pilgrims in 2025 to 9,476 in 2026. The foundation attributed the higher cumulative numbers partly to a longer pilgrimage season and fewer weather-related disruptions. Kedarnath remained operational for 204 days, compared with 175 days last year.

The SDC Foundation report also flagged concerns over pilgrim safety, recording 297 fatalities across the five shrines in 2026, compared with 182 in 2025. Health-related natural deaths alone increased by 81%, from 159 to 288, with Kedarnath accounting for 142 such deaths.

Vehicle movement during the Char Dham Yatra also witnessed a significant rise, increasing from 5,14,016 in 2025 to 6,68,877 in 2026 (till November 14). This represents an increase of 1,54,861 vehicles, or more than 30% over the previous year.

articles.title: Won’t allow hiring of outsiders, hire locals: J&K CM Omar Abdullah to outside companies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts
Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that companies from the outside must hire locals and that hiring outsiders will not be allowed.

“The excuse that trained youths are not available will not work. We will provide you (companies) six months or one year and prepare our youths. We also have ITIs (Industrial Training Institutes), polytechnics, colleges, and universities,” said Mr. Abdullah.
The J&K Chief Minister said youths from J&K have no shortage of talent. “They (youths) only need opportunities. We will not tolerate excuses at the cost of our children’s future,” said Mr. Abdullah.
He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts.

Stating that youngsters from J&K were demonstrating their capabilities in different fields, Mr. Abdullah said, “Wherever you look, you will find young people from J&K serving the country. The moment they get a chance, they leave their mark.”
He said his government was putting in efforts “to ensure development works across the entire region”.

On the current status of Union Territory (UT), Mr. Abdullah said, “We did not become a UT by choice. This situation would never have arisen if it were up to us. The Central Government has put us in this difficult situation. Working under these circumstances is not easy. However, I am not someone who makes excuses based on the prevailing circumstances.”

articles.title: Ruckus erupts between SFI activists and police over setting up bookstalls near Calcutta University
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The SFI leaders said they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a bookstall on the College Street footpath, but police refused on November 16 evening, saying it could disrupt traffic

A ruckus erupted between supporters of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), and police near the University of Kolkata for setting up a book stall. After the clash, police detained several SFI supporters, including the SFI State secretary, Debanjan Dey.

The SFI leadership said that they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a book stall at a makeshift stall on the footpath of College Street. However, the police refused to grant permission on Monday evening, stating that it might disrupt traffic. The book stall was part of a three-day campaign, “Sangrami Boipotro”, by the party. It was supposed to be inaugurated by the Left Front chairman, Biman Bose, on Tuesday evening.

“We have permission from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Jorasanko Police Station for a period of five years to set up bookstalls at College Street. Necessary tax was also paid to the concerned authorities. We have been setting up such stalls for the last four years. Our plan was to do the same this year too. But the Kolkata Police have now refused to allow us anymore,” said Mr. Dey to the media persons

The protesters said that a few police vans had already been stationed on College Street since Monday night. When they began preparing to set up the stalls on Tuesday morning, the police stopped them and said that no book stalls could be organised in the area.

The situation escalated when they blocked College Street and staged a sit-in. They laid out a sheet on the tram line in the middle of the road and began selling their books. They also invited the police to buy books for their children. It immediately resulted in a clash with the police. The police were seen using mild force to disrupt the protesters and clear the road. Several activists, including Mr. Dey, Subhadeep Bandyopadhyay, Didhiti Roy, and Haseeb Hossain, have been detained.

“A heavy police force was deployed across College Street on Tuesday only to stop us selling some books. They have assaulted the students who have been fighting for the books. It is now clear that the government has declared war against the books. They want to destroy the culture and tradition of Bengal. We will have to fight the battle with books only against them,” said Mr. Dey after the detention.
Following the development, the left student union also organised a rally in the evening at the Mahabodhi Society and demanded the immediate release of the detained students.

The dispute over the book stalls set up by the Left parties began during Durga Puja. Police and civic bodies demolished several stalls set up by the parties across Kolkata. In Jadavpur, a bulldozer was also brought in to dismantle a stall, sparking a huge political controversy. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had described Left party supporters as “atheist” and declared that they would not be allowed to set up their book stalls near puja pandals, where such stalls have been a fixture for decades.

A ruckus erupted between supporters of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), and police near the University of Kolkata for setting up a book stall. After the clash, police detained several SFI supporters, including the SFI State secretary, Debanjan Dey.

The SFI leadership said that they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a book stall at a makeshift stall on the footpath of College Street. However, the police refused to grant permission on Monday evening, stating that it might disrupt traffic. The book stall was part of a three-day campaign, “Sangrami Boipotro”, by the party. It was supposed to be inaugurated by the Left Front chairman, Biman Bose, on Tuesday evening.

“We have permission from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Jorasanko Police Station for a period of five years to set up bookstalls at College Street. Necessary tax was also paid to the concerned authorities. We have been setting up such stalls for the last four years. Our plan was to do the same this year too. But the Kolkata Police have now refused to allow us anymore,” said Mr. Dey to the media persons

The protesters said that a few police vans had already been stationed on College Street since Monday night. When they began preparing to set up the stalls on Tuesday morning, the police stopped them and said that no book stalls could be organised in the area.

The situation escalated when they blocked College Street and staged a sit-in. They laid out a sheet on the tram line in the middle of the road and began selling their books. They also invited the police to buy books for their children. It immediately resulted in a clash with the police. The police were seen using mild force to disrupt the protesters and clear the road. Several activists, including Mr. Dey, Subhadeep Bandyopadhyay, Didhiti Roy, and Haseeb Hossain, have been detained.

“A heavy police force was deployed across College Street on Tuesday only to stop us selling some books. They have assaulted the students who have been fighting for the books. It is now clear that the government has declared war against the books. They want to destroy the culture and tradition of Bengal. We will have to fight the battle with books only against them,” said Mr. Dey after the detention.

Following the development, the left student union also organised a rally in the evening at the Mahabodhi Society and demanded the immediate release of the detained students.

articles.title: Convocation ceremony row: Maharaja’s College council asks suspended students to accept their mistake
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The incident caused disrepute to the image of the institution in the public domain, finds inquiry report

A meeting of the council of Maharaja’s College, Kochi, held on Tuesday accepted an inquiry committee report that indicted activists of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) for disrupting a convocation ceremony attended by Minister for Higher Education Roji M. John on October 30.

The meeting recommended that V. Praneel Raj, chairperson, and Nafeesathul Misriya, vice-chairperson of the college union, who were suspended in connection with the incident on November 2, submit an apology admitting their mistake. The inquiry committee report found that the incident had caused disrepute to the image of the institution in the public domain, according to sources.

The council observed that it did not wish to initiate further disciplinary action against the students, but they need to accept their mistake. The meeting took note of the case registered by the police against 10 SFI activists booked in connection with the protest.

SFI activists staged the protest soon after the Minister completed his inaugural address at the convocation ceremony, seeking answers from him on the suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady. The activists demanded that the Minister withdraw his alleged statements against those who were suspended for protesting against Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas. Following the protest, Mr. John had to leave the function midway.

articles.title: U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S.
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner

A senior American soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to U.S. military custody, U.K. police said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The espionage case, the latest involving suspected Kremlin agents in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, comes amid heightened tensions between Moscow and various European capitals after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
It also follows recent security scares at two British air force bases hosting the U.S. military, with officials accusing Iran of involvement in plots to target them.
A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner.

articles.title: Earthshot Prize: Climate action needs innovation, global cooperation, say leaders on green carpet in Mumbai
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations

Global leaders, business executives, and celebrities called for greater investment in environmental innovations and collective action against climate change as they gathered on the green carpet ahead of the Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
Among those attending were former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern, Serum Institute of India CEO Adar Poonawalla, filmmaker Karan Johar, and Maharashtra Environment Minister Pankaja Mund.
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Poonawalla emphasised the importance of supporting environmental innovations and helping them attract investment.

“Prevention is better than cure—that’s what we believe at Serum Institute,” he said, explaining the company’s partnership with the Earthshot Prize. He added that the initiative would help innovators connect with investors and scale up technologies capable of addressing environmental challenges.
Ms. Ardern welcomed the awards to Mumbai, highlighting India’s record of producing the highest number of Earthshot finalists and winners.

“The Earthshot Prize is showcasing responses to that crisis to demonstrate that things are happening and innovation is available, we just need to scale it up with speed,” she said, referring to the climate crisis.

Coral Pasisi, president of Tofia, Niue, highlighted Indigenous-led ocean conservation efforts. “We’re protecting one of the largest areas of ocean on the planet. And we developed a sustainable financing mechanism that’s driven by Indigenous people,” she said, stressing the need for international support.

Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations. She expressed concern that rapid urbanisation and industrialisation had drowned out natural sounds, including birdsong and flowing water, and urged people to protect forests and biodiversity.
Filmmaker Karan Johar praised Prince William’s environmental commitment, describing him as a “climate warrior” who empowered innovators through the Earthshot Prize.

Actor Sonam Kapoor emphasised that environmental responsibility extended beyond public statements. Speaking about her children, she said individuals and governments needed to take concrete steps to protect the environment for future generations.

articles.title: India needs a comprehensive doctrine on space security
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: India’s objective should not be to turn outer space into another arena of conflict, but to ensure that disruption in space does not translate into vulnerability on Earth

Space has transformed from a specialised domain of scientific exploration into an area which hosts essential infrastructure underpinning everyday life, economic activity and national security. Communications, navigation, weather forecasting, disaster management, agriculture, banking, logistics and critical infrastructure are increasingly dependent on satellites and space-enabled services. In India, space capabilities support the armed forces through communications, positioning, surveillance, timing and situational awareness. Space is therefore no longer a separate technological sector but an essential component of national resilience and strategic autonomy. As dependence expands, disruption can have consequences for markets, governance, security and society at large.

The character of threats in space is changing. Competition extends beyond the destruction of satellites to the disruption of the services they provide. Space systems can now be affected by jamming and spoofing that interfere with communications and navigation. Cyber interference can target satellite networks, ground stations and supporting infrastructure, while electronic warfare can degrade signals and reduce the reliability of space-enabled systems. Such methods can produce effects without physically damaging a spacecraft, making attribution and response more complex. The vulnerability lies not only in the satellite itself, but in the wider architecture connecting space assets to users on Earth. This shift from destruction to disruption has made space security a more complex challenge for states.

Science, Space & Environment Report: India needs a comprehensive doctrine on space security. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Transgender rights, healthcare should not be compromised
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Clinical understanding of the care needs of a transgender person remains rudimentary in India. Doctors, nurses, receptionists, security staff and hospital administrators need to be trained in basic transgender health.

Parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 earlier this year. The new Act represents a significant shift from the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019. The 2026 amendment removes the principle of self-identification and demands a medical board’s recommendation; a selection from prescribed categories; and certification by a District Magistrate. It fundamentally changes legal recognition for transgender persons from self-identification to medical assessment. While the 2026 Act does increase protection, it changes the philosophical foundation of transgender rights — from recognition based substantially on autonomy and self-identification towards recognition mediated by medical and administrative authorities.

The definition of “transgender” as introduced in the Amendment Act is in contradiction to established international evidence and guidelines laid down in the World Health Organization ICD-11 and the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care Version 8.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action

Clinical understanding of the care needs of a transgender person remains rudimentary in India. Doctors, nurses, receptionists, security staff and hospital administrators need to be trained in basic transgender health.

Parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 earlier this year. The new Act represents a significant shift from the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019. The 2026 amendment removes the principle of self-identification and demands a medical board’s recommendation; a selection from prescribed categories; and certification by a District Magistrate. It fundamentally changes legal recognition for transgender persons from self-identification to medical assessment. While the 2026 Act does increase protection, it changes the philosophical foundation of transgender rights — from recognition based substantially on autonomy and self-identification towards recognition mediated by medical and administrative authorities.

The definition of “transgender” as introduced in the Amendment Act is in contradiction to established international evidence and guidelines laid down in the World Health Organization ICD-11 and the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care Version 8.

articles.title: Jharkhand SIR: Final BLO meetings at poll stations on November 18
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jharkhand CEO K Ravi Kumar appeals to all eligible Indian citizens in the state to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll by taking part in Ek Aur Avsar (One More Opportunity) camps

Jharkhand Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) K. Ravi Kumar on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) appealed to all eligible Indian citizens in the State to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll being published under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

Speaking to the media in Ranchi, Mr. Ravi asserted that an “Ek Aur Avsar” (One More Opportunity) camp will be held on November 18 at all polling stations in the State, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., where meetings of BLOs (Booth Level Officers) and BLAs-2 (Booth Level Agents-2) will take place in the form of a “Chunav Pathshala” (Electoral Awareness Session).

He pointed out that the objective of this special initiative is to provide one additional opportunity for any eligible Indian citizen who, for various reasons, has not yet had their name added to the electoral roll.

Mr. Ravi explained that the camps will focus primarily on three key areas. First, the Election Commission of India (ECI) is republishing the ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate) list at all polling stations. If any eligible Indian citizen has been included in this list, they may follow the prescribed procedure to submit Form-6 or an enumeration form.

Second, lists of voters in categories such as “No Mapping” or those with “Logical Discrepancies”—who have failed to provide the necessary documentation despite receiving two notices from the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and undergoing a door-to-door verification process—will be made available at the respective polling stations.

Third, efforts are being made to identify eligible Indian citizens who will have turned 18 by October 1, 2026, but who have not yet registered their names in the electoral roll for their respective polling stations. Eligible Indian citizens will be able to have their names included in the electoral roll by submitting Form 6.

The CEO said that this is the sixth and final BLO-BLA-2 meeting being held under the ongoing SIR process in Jharkhand. He urged all eligible citizens in the state to take advantage of this opportunity and get their names added to the electoral roll, ensuring that no eligible Indian citizen remains excluded.

The ECI has already extended the deadline for final publication of electoral rolls in Jharkhand under the SIR to November 30. The final publication was initially scheduled for October 7 and was later extended to October 19 before being revised.

articles.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

articles.title: Telangana’s YTPS final unit commercial operations likely in December 2026, to further boost State’s energy sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana-Genco is implementing a comprehensive action plan to ensure full-scale generation of 4,000 MW through all five units during the coming Rabi and summer season

The 5×800 megawatt Yadadri Thermal Power Station (YTPS) in Damaracherla mandal of Nalgonda district is set to boost Telangana’s power supply position with its fifth 800 MW unit expected to start commercial operations next month.

Of the five 800 MW each units of the power station, four are already generating power and meeting the energy demand of the State. The fifth unit, which was synchronised with the grid on October 20, is set to add to the State’s generating capacity and help meet the demand further.

As part of the efforts to ensure smooth operations at YTPS, the Telangana Power Generation Corporation Ltd (TG-Genco) is implementing a comprehensive action plan to address technical issues in the coal-handling system and ensure full-scale generation of 4,000 MW through all five units during the coming Rabi and summer season.

The YTPS is approaching full operational capacity with the scheduled COD of the fifth unit next month. Although the project faced delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic, forest clearances, railway and land-related issues and directions issued by the National Green Tribunal concerning environmental permissions, the State Government took special measures to accelerate its progress.

Environmental Impact Assessment studies and public hearings were completed afresh and construction activities resumed in February 2024. With continuous government monitoring and effective coordination among officials, four units have already commenced commercial operations.

According to TG-Genco officials, all the major power-generation and ancillary systems at the Yadadri plant, including the boiler, turbine and generator as well as the ash-handling and water-supply systems, are functioning satisfactorily. However, certain technical issues were identified in the coal-handling plant, prompting the government to initiate a special action plan to resolve them.

A high-level team of officials from Bharat Heavy Electronics Limited (BHEL) and TG-Genco led by the Special Chief Secretary (Energy) Vikas Raj and Chairman & Managing Director of the TG-Genco S. Harish camped at the Yadadri plant and formulated an action plan to resolve the technical issues after conducting on-site inspections.

As a result, four coal-feeding lines have been restored with each line capable of supplying an average of 800 tonnes of coal per hour, taking the total coal-handling capacity to 3,200 tonnes per hour. This has significantly reduced interruptions in coal supply and improved the overall performance of the plant.

Alongside addressing the on-site issues, the State Government has adopted a multi-pronged strategy to ensure an uninterrupted supply of coal to the plant. Arrangements have been made to transport three to four coal rakes every day from the Naini coal mine of the Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL) in Odisha. About 4.26 lakh tonnes of coal has been transported from Naini to Yadadri so far.

articles.title: Kerala HC expresses dismay over pending audits at Guruvayur Devaswom Board
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Division Bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji noted that, along with audits pending for the past few years, there was no information on how audits were conducted previously
The Kerala High Court has expressed dismay that the Guruvayur Devaswom Board’s audits for the past few years were incomplete.
The Division Bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji noted that, along with audits pending for the past few years, there was no information on how the audits were conducted previously.
The State informed the court that the audits were completed up to the 2023-24 financial year and that the lack of information from the board had hindered the auditing process of subsequent years.

The court observed that as per the Guruvayur Devaswom Act, the Devaswom Commissioner was responsible for examining the audit reports, identifying any misappropriation of funds and recovering any losses. Accordingly, the court directed the Commissioner to report on the measures adopted to resolve the matter.
The court will consider the matter again on November 20, when the board is expected to file a statement on the future course of its audits.

fullParagraphs: Road development should not be measured only by the number of kilometres constructed or the size of a flyover. We must also ask whether an ordinary person can use that road safely.

Ahead of the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress (IRC), Minister for Roads & Buildings Komatireddy Venkat Reddy speaks about Hyderabad hosting the Indian Roads Congress and the role of modern technology in shaping Telangana’s future.
Hyderabad is hosting the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress. What does this mean for Telangana?

It is one of the most important national platforms where experts discuss the future of road and bridge construction, maintenance and development. More than 3,500 road sector experts from different parts of India and abroad are participating. For us, it is an opportunity to bring the latest technologies and expertise to the State.
What can delegates and the people of Telangana expect from the four-day event?

Around 400 exhibition stalls will showcase modern road-construction machinery, innovative materials, equipment and technologies from Indian and international companies. The Telangana pavilion will present the State’s ongoing road, bridge, building and infrastructure projects, along with our future development plans.
Road development is often measured in terms of kilometres constructed and money spent. You have repeatedly spoken about the ‘Right to Walk’. Why is this important?

How will the discussions and technology exhibition at the IRC translate into practical benefits for Telangana?

Road construction is changing rapidly. Artificial intelligence, digital monitoring, new construction materials and climate-resilient engineering can improve the quality, safety and lifespan of roads. The conference can open doors for partnerships, investment and better construction practices.

articles.title: India, Japan set to review defence ties as Rajnath, Jaishankar arrive in Tokyo
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The two-day visit comes a day after the Quad leaders' summit in Manila, Philippines and as India hosts a joint humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) exercise involving the four member countries

India and Japan are set to review their bilateral defence ties and strategic cooperation as Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar arrived in Tokyo on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) for the fourth edition of the 2+2 ministerial dialogue.

Mr. Singh and Mr. Jaishankar will co-chair the Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue (2+2) with their Japanese counterparts, Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement.

The two-day visit comes a day after the Quad leaders' summit in Manila, Philippines and as India hosts a joint humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) exercise involving the four member countries.

The Quad, comprising India, the U.S., Japan and Australia, is a strategic grouping focused on promoting a free, open and rules-based Indo-Pacific through cooperation in maritime security, technology, infrastructure and disaster response.
The India-Japan 2+2 dialogue follows the previous round held in New Delhi on August 20, 2024.

India and Japan will review the full range of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, exchange views on regional and global developments and reaffirm their shared commitment to a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, the MEA said.
The two sides are expected to discuss defence equipment and technology, maritime security, joint military exercises across all three services and defence industrial partnerships, it said.
Mr. Singh will also hold a bilateral meeting with Mr. Koizumi, while Mr. Jaishankar will hold the 19th India-Japan Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue with Motegi.

The meeting between Mr. Singh and Mr. Koizumi will be their third this year, following their engagements in New Delhi in August and on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus in Cebu in October.
In a post on X ahead of the visit, Mr. Singh said India and Japan shared a common vision for a "free, open, and rules-based Indo-Pacific", grounded in mutual trust and democratic values.

articles.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Akvan likely to cross between Machilipatnam and Puri, says APSDMA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The storm picked up speed to 7 kmph over the past six hours. It was about 580 km from Visakhapatnam, 590 km from Machilipatnam and 710 km from Gopalpur in Odisha

Cyclone Akvan is now likely to cross the coast between Machilipatnam and Puri, along the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts, around noon on Friday (November 20) as a severe cyclonic storm, the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) said in an update at 12.10 p.m. on Wednesday.
The storm picked up speed to 7 kmph over the past six hours. It was about 580 km from Visakhapatnam, 590 km from Machilipatnam and 710 km from Gopalpur in Odisha, APSDMA said.
The authority asked people in the north coastal districts to stay alert. -- The Hindu Bureau

articles.title: Democrat Peltola wins in Alaska, securing 56-44 U.S. Senate majority
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Alaska’s isolated communities can make its election counts unusually lengthy. The race was further complicated by allegations that Democrats helped recruit an independent candidate as a spoiler

Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska’s U.S. Senate race on Tuesday (November 17), ​projections from U.S. media showed, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and giving her ‌party its ninth flip of the midterm elections and ​a commanding 56-44 Senate majority.
Ms. Peltola won 50% of first-place ⁠votes to Mr. Sullivan’s 46%, enough to clear the 50% threshold and avoid additional rounds under Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system.

President Donald Trump won Alaska by 13 percentage ‌points in the 2024 presidential election, but voter frustration with the high cost of living and the state’s strong independent political streak ‌put it back in play for Democrats.
U.S. Senator Dan S. Sullivan | Photo Credit: Getty Images via AFP

“As a lifelong ‌Alaskan ⁠who has dedicated my career to serving our state, ⁠there is no greater honour than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first,” Ms. Peltola said on X ​after media projected her victory. “Thank ‌you, Alaska. Let’s get to work.”
Alaska’s isolated communities can make its election counts unusually lengthy. The race was further complicated by allegations that Democrats helped recruit an independent candidate as a spoiler.
Two ‌other candidates were on the general-election ballot: Republican Gerry Heikes, ​a drywall contractor, and Dan J. Sullivan Jr., a retired schoolteacher running as an independent.

Republicans alleged that ⁠Mr. Sullivan Jr. was recruited to confuse voters who supported the incumbent senator and unsuccessfully sought to remove him from the ballot, arguing he was ‌not a “good faith” candidate. Alaska’s Supreme Court rejected that argument.

Just before Election Day, the New York Times reported that Ms. Peltola’s campaign had helped recruit Mr. Sullivan Jr. into the race. Ms. Peltola’s campaign denied any involvement. Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy ordered a State investigation into the allegations and has said it was examining anything that could “resemble perjury.”
The ‌Justice Department also launched a criminal investigation into possible wrongdoing. U.S. Attorney ​General Todd Blanche has described the reported recruitment effort as “fraud.”

Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska’s U.S. Senate race on Tuesday (November 17), ​projections from U.S. media showed, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and giving her ‌party its ninth flip of the midterm elections and ​a commanding 56-44 Senate majority.

Ms. Peltola won 50% of first-place ⁠votes to Mr. Sullivan’s 46%, enough to clear the 50% threshold and avoid additional rounds under Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system.

President Donald Trump won Alaska by 13 percentage ‌points in the 2024 presidential election, but voter frustration with the high cost of living and the state’s strong independent political streak ‌put it back in play for Democrats.

U.S. Senator Dan S. Sullivan | Photo Credit: Getty Images via AFP

“As a lifelong ‌Alaskan ⁠who has dedicated my career to serving our state, ⁠there is no greater honour than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first,” Ms. Peltola said on X ​after media projected her victory. “Thank ‌you, Alaska. Let’s get to work.”

Alaska’s isolated communities can make its election counts unusually lengthy. The race was further complicated by allegations that Democrats helped recruit an independent candidate as a spoiler.

Two ‌other candidates were on the general-election ballot: Republican Gerry Heikes, ​a drywall contractor, and Dan J. Sullivan Jr., a retired schoolteacher running as an independent.

Republicans alleged that ⁠Mr. Sullivan Jr. was recruited to confuse voters who supported the incumbent senator and unsuccessfully sought to remove him from the ballot, arguing he was ‌not a “good faith” candidate. Alaska’s Supreme Court rejected that argument.

Just before Election Day, the New York Times reported that Ms. Peltola’s campaign had helped recruit Mr. Sullivan Jr. into the race. Ms. Peltola’s campaign denied any involvement. Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy ordered a State investigation into the allegations and has said it was examining anything that could “resemble perjury.”

The ‌Justice Department also launched a criminal investigation into possible wrongdoing. U.S. Attorney ​General Todd Blanche has described the reported recruitment effort as “fraud.”

articles.title: China’s Xi, other leaders say Asia-Pacific must embrace open trade and fair growth
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In a CEO Summit on the sidelines of the APEC Summit, the Chinese President did not mention export controls, Nvidia or the U.S. directly

The Asia-Pacific must pursue more open trade and equitable growth if it is to remain stable and dynamic, Chinese President Xi Jinping told business executives gathered on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in the southern Chinese technology and financial hub of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit.

U.S. President Donald Trump was due to join other leaders later for the APEC leaders' summit, travelling from the Philippines, where he attended an annual summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

Mr. Trump's “America First” approach of tariff hikes and other moves runs counter to APEC's aim of eventually forming a Pacific Rim free trade zone. U.S. limits on Chinese access to leading-edge American technology, such as the Nvidia computer chips that help to power artificial intelligence, are a constant source of strain with Beijing.
Mr. Xi and other APEC leaders called for a more open approach, without directly criticising the U.S. shift toward protecting its own markets.
The summit is showcasing Shenzhen, which China has transformed in the past four decades from a fishing village into a skyscraper-studded centre for export manufacturing and technology.

China's ascent as the second-largest economy hinged on global investments and access to world markets as global manufacturers shifted factories overseas to tap into cheaper labour and faster-growing markets. “China will not only cut tariffs and expand market access, but also go a step further. We will carry out reform in challenging areas such as rules, regulation, and standards,” Mr. Xi told the CEO summit, reiterating Beijing's pledges to improve conditions for global investors.

“While pursuing its own development, China has shared opportunities with other countries and worked for common development,” he said. “It has steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation.”
Mr. Xi's speech highlighted China's aim to lead global industrial transformation, said George Chen, partner and chair of Digital Practice at The Asia Group.

“While he didn't say so explicitly, his message was clear: China wants to be seen as a partner in global technology development, in contrast to Washington's more restrictive approach,” Mr. Chen said, noting that Xi did not mention export controls, Nvidia or the U.S. directly.

Mr. Xi faces pressure at home from slowing growth as retail spending and investment have dragged as China endures a prolonged property market slump. The economy is still growing at a rate of more than 4%, but that's mainly due to surging exports that are provoking a backlash among many of China's trading partners. China's trade surplus for this year is on track to exceed $1 trillion for a second year in a row.

articles.title: Xi, Putin meet ahead of historic Trump trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Washington had signalled that Ukraine — something Mr. Xi vehemently sees as not China's problem — was not expected to be addressed, before Mr. Trump said that it would

Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin began talks in Shenzhen on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), a day ahead of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.

Thursday's (November 19) trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could decide the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence.
Washington had signalled that Ukraine — something Mr. Xi vehemently sees as not China's problem — was not expected to be addressed, before Mr. Trump said that it would.

China has said only that the leaders would hold "in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations" on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting.
Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a U.S.-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.
Beijing has long maintained that the U.S. and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

Chinese and Russian news agencies reported at around noon on Wednesday (November 18) that Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin had met for talks — the fifth time the two leaders have met this year, including once by video link.
Mr. Putin has been shunned by the West since launching Europe's worst conflict since World War II with his 2022 attack on Ukraine.
Addressing the APEC gathering on Wednesday (November 18), he said he expected the trilateral summit with Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump to be "highly useful".
"At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums," Mr. Putin said.

articles.title: Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The approval is valid from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027, and is expected to help Nepal manage the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic generation

Nepal has received approval to import up to 350 MW of electricity from India this winter to meet domestic power demand amid a decline in hydropower generation and damage to several projects caused by recent floods.

The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) under India's Ministry of Power has authorised the Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA), the State-owned power utility, to procure electricity at competitive rates from the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) for up to 17 hours a day, NEA officials said.

The approval is valid from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027, and is expected to help Nepal manage the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic generation, NEA Managing Director Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha said.

Of the approved 350 MW, Nepal can import 300 MW through the Kataiya-Kushaha, Ramnagar-Surajpura and Raxaul-Parwanipur transmission lines. The remaining 50 MW can be sourced through the New Nautanwa-Mainahiya transmission line.
Nepal's dependence on run-of-the-river hydropower projects makes electricity generation highly seasonal.

While rising river flows during the summer months enable the country to generate surplus power for export, mainly to India, declining water levels during winter significantly reduce domestic production, forcing it to rely on imports.
The country's power supply situation has also been affected by the damage caused to several hydropower projects in central Nepal during the devastating Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods in August.
Projects with a combined installed capacity of 431 MW have remained disconnected from the national grid following the disaster.

However, domestic generation is expected to improve from mid-April as water levels in rivers gradually rise, reducing Nepal's dependence on imported electricity and potentially allowing it to resume exports, officials said.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18: What does it mean?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means

NASA’s Voyager 1 is set to cross a historic threshold in space exploration as it is about to become humanity’s first object to reach one light-day from Earth. The iconic probe, which has travelled farther from Earth than any other human-made object since its launch in 1977, is expected to cross the landmark on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (3:46:07 p.m. IST), according to NASA.
Infographics: Voyager I’s 49-year journey into the void
Having spent 49 years, two months and 11 days hurtling through the cosmos, Voyager 1 continues to push the boundaries of human space exploration.

One light-day is a staggering measure of distance, rather than a measure of time. It represents the exact space that light, which travels at roughly 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometres) per second, covers in a full 24-hour period.
For Voyager 1, this is equivalent to more than 16 billion miles away from Earth.
When Voyager 1 reaches that incredible milestone on November 18, its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth — in other words, one light-day.

Sunlight takes just over eight minutes to reach Earth, and over four hours and 10 minutes to reach Neptune. From November 18, any radio command sent from NASA’s Deep Space Network to Voyager 1 will take a full 24 hours to arrive, requiring another 24 hours for the spacecraft’s response to return.

Launched on September 2, 1977, Voyager 1 was originally designed for a four-year mission to study Jupiter and Saturn. Its trajectory eventually allowed it to overtake its twin, Voyager 2, which was launched 16 days earlier. According to NASA, Voyager 2 is expected to reach the one-light-day distance from Earth in November 2035.

The two spacecrafts were launched to explore the outer planets, with Voyager 1 taking a trajectory that eventually carried it towards interstellar space. It became the first spacecraft that entered the interstellar space in August 2012 and has continued transmitting information from beyond the solar system. Today, it speeds onward at roughly 38,000 miles per hour.
In 1990, Voyager 1 captured the most distant image of Earth, known as the iconic “Pale Blue Dot,” while venturing farther than any other human-made object beyond Neptune.
