fullParagraphs: Suri: The Seventh Note by Tathvamasi Studios is set in a universe controlled by evil music. The game was launched in October

The story of Suri: The Seventh Note, a 2D video game by Bengaluru-based Tathvamasi Studios, is set in a world corrupted by an evil version of music. Everything in this universe moves in tune with that nefarious sonic presence. The protagonist, Ajira, must find a fruit located at the centre of the island to save her mother from certain death. Soon, she realises her actions shall determine the fate of the island itself.

Suri: The Seventh Note is the brainchild of Glen Martin from Kochi, founder of Tathvamasi Studios, who is also the game director of the video. He is joined by Chitrak Srivastava, co-founder and the game’s art director. The game was launched on Playstation Store and Steam, in October for PlayStations and PCs.

Glen, formerly a data scientist, found himself immersed in game-making during the pandemic. He began by making smaller games, with friends from different places joining him on a Discord server to help. “When we started to build the game, it was not meant to be a project. But once we realised its potential, we began to think about what could be unique about this game,” says Glen.
Glen Martin and Chitrak Srivastava | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

“At that point, I was playing a parry-focused combat game called Sekiro. It’s a very hard game, and I am not good at it. But then I saw a lot of streamers play the game skilfully, without even taking a single hit, and I realised that when the game is played at that level, it has a certain rhythmic quality to it,” he adds. “The sounds of the sword clinking, the jumps and movements, everything felt choreographed.”
This ultimately led him to turn Suri… into a rhythm platformer game.

Suri... is a mix of two different games: rhythm and platformer. Rhythm games are music-themed action games that assess a player’s sense of timing and metre, while platformers are a sub-genre where a main character moves through uneven terrain and suspended platforms.

“There are very few games that I’ve done this before, so our well of references was limited. In Suri..., the world moves to the rhythm. All the things that you would normally interact with in a regular platformer, like traps, obstacles, etc., are all tied to the rhythm in our game. You have to listen to the music to understand when a thing would move up and down or when a leaf would open or close and so on,” explains Glen. “When done well, it feels like dancing through levels.”

In 2024, Suri was one of five games at the inaugural edition of PlayStation’s India Hero Project, an incubator programme from Sony Interactive Entertainment. This ultimately allowed Glen to quit his job and hire more people.
A still from Suri: The Seventh Note | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

articles.title: One in five women in parts of Northeast deficient in vitamin B1: ICMR-NIN study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Vitamin B1 or Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function

Around one in five pregnant and lactating women in Assam’s Barak Valley and adjoining districts of Tripura suffer from suboptimal levels of ‘Thiamine’ (vitamin B1), according to a study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN), Hyderabad, highlighting a continuing public health concern in the region.

The study, ‘Re-Emergence of Thiamine Deficiency Among Pregnant and Lactating Women in Northeast India’, published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, examined the prevalence of thiamine deficiency and its link to dietary practices in areas where beriberi cases have previously been reported, said a press release on Monday.

Researchers conducted the community-based study during 2023-24 among 1,083 women from 120 villages in Assam’s Barak Valley and neighbouring parts of Tripura. Thiamine status was assessed using biochemical and functional indicators to determine the extent of deficiency.

The findings showed that about 20% of participants had inadequate thiamine levels. Based on blood thiamine measurements, 4.9% were deficient, and 15.2% had marginal levels. A separate functional assessment produced similar results, with 8.5% showing severe deficiency and 12.1% marginal deficiency. Pregnant women were found to be more vulnerable than lactating mothers.

Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function. Deficiency can lead to serious health complications, making adequate intake particularly important during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

According to Mahesh Kumar Mummadi, NIN scientist and lead author of the study, dietary assessments revealed that most women consumed rice-based diets with limited diversity. Practices such as consuming stored rice, repeatedly washing rice before cooking, chewing betel nut and drinking salted tea were associated with a higher risk of deficiency.

NIN director Bharati Kulkarni said the findings underscore the need to look beyond routinely monitored nutrients in maternal health programmes. She called for greater dietary diversity, regular nutritional surveillance and targeted supplementation in high-risk regions. Researchers also noted that since the study focused on areas with previously reported beriberi clusters, the findings may not be representative of all pregnant and lactating women across India.

• The study, ‘Re-Emergence of Thiamine Deficiency Among Pregnant and Lactating Women in Northeast India’, published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, examined the prevalence of thiamine deficiency and its link to dietary practices in areas where beriberi cases have previously been reported, said a press release on Monday.

articles.title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves cash rewards for information on weapons looted by Maoists
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The decision comes amid the State government’s efforts to eliminate Left-wing extremism and accelerate development in areas previously affected by Maoist activities

The Maharashtra Cabinet on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) approved a cash reward scheme for individuals providing information leading to the recovery of weapons looted by Maoists from security forces, with rewards of up to ₹1.5 lakh for individual weapons and sanctioning powers extending to ₹1 crore. The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.

According to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), the reward amount will depend on the type and number of weapons recovered, including automatic and semi-automatic firearms, other weapons and ammunition.

The government said Maoists had, over the years, looted weapons belonging to State security forces during attacks on police stations and police personnel. While existing provisions provide rewards for information leading to the arrest of Maoists and additional financial assistance to those surrendering with weapons, there was no specific provision for rewarding individuals who helped recover weapons previously looted from security forces.
The Home Department subsequently proposed a separate reward mechanism to facilitate the recovery of these weapons, which received Cabinet approval on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

Under the scheme, Superintendents of Police will have the authority to sanction rewards of up to ₹10 lakh, while the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Gadchiroli Range, can approve amounts exceeding ₹10 lakh and up to ₹25 lakh.

Rewards exceeding ₹25 lakh and up to ₹50 lakh will require approval from the Special Inspector General of Police, Anti-Naxal Operations, while the Additional Director General of Police (Special Operations) will be authorised to approve rewards exceeding ₹50 lakh and up to ₹1 crore.
The decision comes amid the State government’s efforts to eliminate Left-wing extremism and accelerate development in areas previously affected by Maoist activities.

In its statement, the government said coordinated efforts by the Centre and the State had weakened the influence of Maoist organisations in the region, particularly in Gadchiroli and Gondia, which it described as having become Naxal-free.
The government also said several development projects were being implemented in these districts as part of efforts to transform areas previously affected by Left-wing extremism.

articles.title: Three Hyderabad shopping streets feature in APAC’s retail rankings, Delhi’s Khan Market tops India’s retail streets with ₹1,875/sft rental
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jubilee Hills leads Hyderabad’s retail areas with ₹250/sft monthly rental. It is ₹230/sft in Banjara Hills and ₹225/sft in Himayatnagar

Three of Hyderabad’s prominent shopping destinations — Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Himayatnagar — have featured in the Asia-Pacific (APAC) rankings of the world’s leading retail streets, according to the latest report by global real estate consultancy Cushman and Wakefield.

The figures offer an indication of the rental costs associated with securing retail space in some of Hyderabad’s established shopping districts. Jubilee Hills secured the 51st position in the regional rankings, with prime retail rents estimated at ₹250 per square feet per month. Banjara Hills and Himayatnagar jointly occupied the 52nd position, with corresponding rents of ₹230 and ₹225 per square feet per month, respectively.

For instance, renting a 1,000 square feet outlet in Jubilee Hills would translate into an indicative monthly rental expenditure of ₹2.5 lakh, compared with ₹2.3 lakh in Banjara Hills and ₹2.25 lakh in Himayatnagar.
The findings are part of the 36th edition of Cushman and Wakefield’s ‘Main Streets Across the World 2026’ report, which examines headline rents across 147 leading retail locations globally.

Hyderabad’s three shopping destinations feature alongside several other Indian retail streets in the APAC rankings, reflecting the representation of multiple Indian cities among the region’s prominent retail markets.

Delhi’s Khan Market retained its position as India’s highest-ranked retail street, occupying the 25th position in APAC and 24th globally. Its headline rents increased 14% year-on-year to approximately ₹1,875 per square feet per month. Mumbai’s Linking Road ranked 33rd, with monthly rents of ₹1,175 per sq. ft. It also recorded the highest rental growth across Asia-Pacific at 28% year-on-year.

Other Indian retail destinations featured in the rankings included Vittal Mallya Road, Brigade Road and Indiranagar in Bengaluru, JM Road, MG Road and FC Road in Pune, Park Street and Gariahat in Kolkata and Anna Nagar and Pondy Bazaar in Chennai.

The report identified India as the strongest-performing market in the Asia-Pacific region, with several high streets recording double-digit rental growth. Prime retail rents across APAC increased 3.1% year-on-year in the 12 months to the third quarter of 2026, compared with 2.3% in the corresponding period a year earlier.

“India’s retail market continues to demonstrate strong fundamentals, supported by resilient consumption, sustained retailer expansion and increasing premiumisation,” said Milin Rohinesh, head of Retail-India at Cushman and Wakefield.

At the global level, New York City’s Upper Fifth Avenue reclaimed its position as the world’s most expensive retail street, with rents increasing 35% over the past year to US$2,700 per square feet annually. Three of Hyderabad’s prominent shopping destinations — Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Himayatnagar — have featured in the Asia-Pacific (APAC) rankings of the world’s leading retail streets, according to the latest report by global real estate consultancy Cushman and Wakefield.

The figures offer an indication of the rental costs associated with securing retail space in some of Hyderabad’s established shopping districts. Jubilee Hills secured the 51st position in the regional rankings, with prime retail rents estimated at ₹250 per square feet per month. Banjara Hills and Himayatnagar jointly occupied the 52nd position, with corresponding rents of ₹230 and ₹225 per square feet per month, respectively.

For instance, renting a 1,000 square feet outlet in Jubilee Hills would translate into an indicative monthly rental expenditure of ₹2.5 lakh, compared with ₹2.3 lakh in Banjara Hills and ₹2.25 lakh in Himayatnagar.

The findings are part of the 36th edition of Cushman and Wakefield’s ‘Main Streets Across the World 2026’ report, which examines headline rents across 147 leading retail locations globally.

Hyderabad’s three shopping destinations feature alongside several other Indian retail streets in the APAC rankings, reflecting the representation of multiple Indian cities among the region’s prominent retail markets.

Delhi’s Khan Market retained its position as India’s highest-ranked retail street, occupying the 25th position in APAC and 24th globally. Its headline rents increased 14% year-on-year to approximately ₹1,875 per square feet per month. Mumbai’s Linking Road ranked 33rd, with monthly rents of ₹1,175 per sq. ft. It also recorded the highest rental growth across Asia-Pacific at 28% year-on-year.

Other Indian retail destinations featured in the rankings included Vittal Mallya Road, Brigade Road and Indiranagar in Bengaluru, JM Road, MG Road and FC Road in Pune, Park Street and Gariahat in Kolkata and Anna Nagar and Pondy Bazaar in Chennai.

The report identified India as the strongest-performing market in the Asia-Pacific region, with several high streets recording double-digit rental growth. Prime retail rents across APAC increased 3.1% year-on-year in the 12 months to the third quarter of 2026, compared with 2.3% in the corresponding period a year earlier.

“India’s retail market continues to demonstrate strong fundamentals, supported by resilient consumption, sustained retailer expansion and increasing premiumisation,” said Milin Rohinesh, head of Retail-India at Cushman and Wakefield.

At the global level, New York City’s Upper Fifth Avenue reclaimed its position as the world’s most expensive retail street, with rents increasing 35% over the past year to US$2,700 per square feet annually. The street moved from third position in 2025 to first, reclaiming the top spot for the first time since 2023.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court ruled that the 24-hour custody limit under Article 22(2) of the Indian Constitution begins when a person’s liberty is curtailed during detention, not from the formal arrest

The story so far: The Supreme Court on November 5, 2026, held that the 24 hours timeline as mandated under clause (2) of Article 22 of the Constitution of India would commence from the date and time of a person’s detention when their liberty is curtailed and not from the time of their formal arrest.

A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S. Chandurkar examined the Article 22(2) of the Constitution which says that every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate and no such person shall be detained in custody beyond the said period without the authority of a magistrate.

articles.title: Eight interns of Kolkata Medical College issued show-cause over statements on Chorbagan stampede
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The interns had raised questions about the government’s decision to shift the injured persons to a private hospital after the Chorbagan stampede. The State government has said decision was taken in the interest of the patients

The West Bengal Health Department has issued show-cause notices to eight intern doctors of the Medical College in Kolkata for making statements to the media regarding the alleged mismanagement at the hospital during the Chorbagan stampede incident.

Nineteen people died — most of them women and children — and 25 were injured after a stampede broke out at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata on October 16, 2026. The injured were immediately rushed to Medical College, Kolkata, from where some of them were also shifted to a private hospital later.

Two days after the incident, some junior doctors and interns organised a press conference , in which they said that this tragedy exposed the “sorry state of affairs” at a premier tertiary care hospital in Bengal.

They said the hospital lacked a trauma care centre, the emergency ward lacked essential medicines, and the neurosurgery department was ill-equipped to handle critical cases. The government’s decision to shift the injured persons to a private hospital amounted to the State admitting its healthcare system was in a shambles, they said. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said decision was taken in the interest of the patients.

Following the development, the government has now issued show-cause notices to eight of the interns who attended the press conference. It has been alleged that they were making statements to the media, neglecting their duties at a critical time. One of the interns who received the notice told the media that the government asked to respond to the notice in three days.

“They said that our statement was misleading, as an inquiry found all the medicines in stock and other infrastructure in place. We have been asked why were not on duty. To be clear, I did not have duty in the roaster that day,” he said.

After the stampede and remarks of intern doctors, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari ordered the health department to investigate why the junior doctors were holding press conferences instead of being in the hospital ward during working hours.

articles.title: Madurai Tanishq showroom gold heist: Police recover all the burgled gold, diamond jewellery
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Special teams went through the video footage of more than 100 CCTV cameras in Madurai and other districts to make the breakthrough, City Police Commissioner S. Rajendiran says after inspecting the recovered ornaments
All the 11.384 kg of gold and diamond ornaments, stolen from Tanishq showroom in Madurai five days ago , has been recovered intact, said Commissioner of Police S. Rajendiran.

After inspecting the recovered ornaments on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), Mr. Rajendiran said three accused, S. Nishanth , his father Suresh and friend Meenakshi, had been arrested and a two-wheeler seized. “ Suresh and Meenakshi had knowledge about Nishanth’s involvement in the burglary that took place on November 12 but did not inform the police. Besides, Meenakshi was aware of the spot where the gold was buried,” he added.

The possible involvement of any other person, including showroom insider, or those who helped Nishanth during his run, would be investigated when they were taken into police custody for interrogation, he said.

Mr. Rajendiran said special teams had gone through video footages of over 100 of CCTV cameras in Madurai and other districts to crack the case. “The CCTV footages of the November 5 recce by Nishanth [by climbing up the terrace of the showroom] gave the actual breakthrough. Besides, [footage of] the tattoo on his hand, and social media posts [with his photographs] that went viral helped the police nab him,” the Commissioner said.

Mr. Rajendiran also clarified on the difference between the quantum of valuables that was initially reported and the recovery of 11.384 kg. Initially, the showroom staff made a rough estimate. However, after the final assessment with the showroom stock, the quantum of property lost came down to 11.384 kg, he said.

He also revealed that Nishanth was involved in a fatal accident in Madurai in 2023. Nishanth, who was in deep debt, planned to strike at Tanishq showroom in view of the incomplete construction works in the building.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) A.G. Inigo Thivyan was present during the press briefing.
Nishanth, who was arrested by a police team in Dharmapuri district on Monday (November 16), was brought to Madurai late in the night and grilled by senior police officers, including Mr. Thivyan.

Based on his confession, the police took him to a secluded place in Madakulam and recovered a cache of the booty which was left buried, a police officer told The Hindu . The police had already recovered over 5 kg of the stolen ornaments after the arrest of Suresh and Meenakshi.
Later, Nishanth was produced before a Judicial Magistrate and remanded in judicial custody till December 1.

Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the Iran-backed group toward the Riyadh area.

articles.title: Gilead signs generic licensing deals for experimental Ebola drug
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A late-stage trial is testing the drug in people at high risk after exposure. The deals are intended to line up manufacturing and supply before trial results and regulatory filings

Gilead Sciences said on Monday it had signed royalty-free deals with three generic drugmakers to make its experimental Ebola prevention drug available in 127 mainly low- and lower-middle-income countries if it succeeds in trials and wins regulatory approvals.

The deals with Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories, Eva Pharma and Ferozsons Laboratories cover obeldesivir, and include all African countries reporting cases in the current Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak. Obeldesivir has shown activity against several Ebola-related viruses in preclinical studies but is not approved for any use in any country.
A late-stage trial is testing the drug in people at high risk after exposure. The deals are intended to line up manufacturing and supply before trial results and regulatory filings.

Gilead is also expanding remdesivir licences to cover Ebola-related diseases if trial results are positive and regulators approve the drug. The company has donated more than 38,000 remdesivir vials to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and Kenya, including more than 2,000 recently sent to Kenya for investigational treatment and post-exposure prevention.
Remdesivir is not approved to treat or prevent Ebola Bundibugyo disease, and its clinical effectiveness has not been established.

articles.title: Plea in SC asks how many voters have filled enumeration forms to get back on electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Petitioners seek disclosure of the number of ASDD voters who have submitted enumeration forms and want those who used Form 6 to retain their old EPIC numbers

A fresh petition has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking disclosure of the number of Delhi voters whose names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls under the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) categories but who subsequently submitted enumeration forms to be restored to the voter list.
The petitioners have also sought an extension of the provision allowing such voters to submit enumeration forms and the restoration of their old Electoral Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers.

Filed on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) by transparency rights activists Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri, the petition argues that ASDD voters who have already submitted Form 6 should also be allowed to fill enumeration forms.

This, they said, would ensure that they are restored to the electoral rolls with their existing EPIC numbers instead of being classified as new voters. Form 6 is intended for registering new voters but had also been used by those whose names were deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

During an earlier hearing, the Supreme Court had termed the use of Form 6 by voters excluded from the draft rolls under the ASDD category an “error”, as the form requires applicants to declare that they are first-time voters.

Subsequently, the Election Commission of India issued a directive allowing voters marked as ASDD in seven States, including Delhi, where the SIR is under way, to submit enumeration forms again instead of using Form 6. These voters had been excluded because their issued enumeration forms were not received back.
The petition has also raised concerns over the alleged misuse of Form 7 for targeted deletions. It has sought an audit and public disclosure of all Form 7 applications submitted so far.

The petitioners have further requested that booth-level agents (BLAs) of political parties filing Form 7 be required to identify themselves as party representatives rather than submitting applications only under their individual names.

A fresh petition has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking disclosure of the number of Delhi voters whose names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls under the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) categories but who subsequently submitted enumeration forms to be restored to the voter list.

The petitioners have also sought an extension of the provision allowing such voters to submit enumeration forms and the restoration of their old Electoral Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers.

Filed on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) by transparency rights activists Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri, the petition argues that ASDD voters who have already submitted Form 6 should also be allowed to fill enumeration forms.

This, they said, would ensure that they are restored to the electoral rolls with their existing EPIC numbers instead of being classified as new voters. Form 6 is intended for registering new voters but had also been used by those whose names were deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

During an earlier hearing, the Supreme Court had termed the use of Form 6 by voters excluded from the draft rolls under the ASDD category an “error”, as the form requires applicants to declare that they are first-time voters.

Subsequently, the Election Commission of India issued a directive allowing voters marked as ASDD in seven States, including Delhi, where the SIR is under way, to submit enumeration forms again instead of using Form 6. These voters had been excluded because their issued enumeration forms were not received back.

The petition has also raised concerns over the alleged misuse of Form 7 for targeted deletions. It has sought an audit and public disclosure of all Form 7 applications submitted so far.

The petitioners have further requested that booth-level agents (BLAs) of political parties filing Form 7 be required to identify themselves as party representatives rather than submitting applications only under their individual names.

articles.title: Eknath Shinde tears Sonia Gandhi’s book over Savarkar references, seeks ban in Maharashtra
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party has demanded that publisher HarperCollins withdraw two pages from the memoir, while the Congress condemned the protest and Uddhav Sena leaders hit back at the Shinde faction

Shiv Sena’s Eknath Shinde on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) tore pages from Sonia Gandhi’s memoir ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, demanding that the publisher withdraw two pages that the party claimed contained objectionable references to Vinayak Damodar Savarkar.

“We have torn the pages of the book as a mark of protest against the statements on Savarkar ji. We have sought that Harper Collins, the publisher, should scrap these two pages. Till they do that, we have sought that the Maharashtra government ban the sale of the book in the State. We will soon write to the government to seek a ban,” Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Nirupam told The Hindu .
He was among the six party spokespersons who addressed a press conference on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). The Shiv Sena is part of the ruling Mahayuti alliance in Maharashtra.

The Congress hit back at the Sena, condemning the act as “shameful”. “It shows intellectual bankruptcy. I feel pity for them. When you spit at the sun, the spit lands on you. It is a condemnable act,” Maharashtra Congress president Harshawardhan Sapkal said.

Former Chief Minister Prithviraj Chavan termed the act “childish”. “We are not the Taliban. We believe in the Constitution of Babasaheb Ambedkar. Everyone has the right to express their opinion. If you do not accept her views or if you think there are factual inaccuracies, refute them or point them out or write a separate book. But tearing a book is childishness,” he said.

Meanwhile, Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC tore a photograph bearing the image of Balasaheb Thackeray during the press conference. When this was pointed out to her, she was seen slipping the torn photograph under a pile of papers. She later justified the act, saying that the photograph showed Balasaheb Thackeray slapping an effigy of Manishankar Aiyar with a chappal.

“This is what he has taught us. We have only torn the pages of a book,” she said. She was later summoned by Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. After the meeting, he said there was no question of anyone insulting Balasaheb Thackeray.
“He is venerable for us. Nobody can insult him,” Mr. Shinde said.

Meanwhile, the Uddhav Sena staged protests at several places in Maharashtra, including Mumbai. The issue also triggered a backlash in the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), where Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Kishori Pednekar engaged in a heated exchange with Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde.
The Shiv Sena said the references to Savarkar appeared on pages 201 and 443 of the book.

articles.title: Bombay HC sets aside ICICI Bank Board of Directors’ sanction order on Chanda Kochhar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court held that the Reserve Bank of India constitutes the authority with jurisdiction under Section 36-AA(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to grant permission

A sanction order, dated May 15, 2023, issued by the Board of Directors of ICICI Bank to prosecute Chanda Kochhar, was set aside by Justice Milind N. Jadhav of the Bombay High Court, who held that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) constitutes the authority with jurisdiction under Section 36-AA(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, to grant permission.

Section 36-AA(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 states that the RBI possesses the power to remove a Chairperson, Director, or an officer from a bank, and because the power of removal vests with the RBI, the Board of Directors cannot act as the authority to grant sanction, the judge noted. The RBI did not pass an order of removal against the petitioner, and the petitioner had lost the opportunity to make a representation to the RBI against a removal order, Justice Jadhav said.

Justice Jadhav stated that nullity of sanction goes to the root of prosecution in proceedings under the Prevention of Corruption Act as it is a fact relating to jurisdiction and it stands on a pedestal as an absence of sanction, adding that the Board of Directors failed to examine evidence and material collected by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) before granting permission.

The petitioner served as the Managing Director of ICICI Bank when the CBI registered a report in 2019 regarding loans sanctioned to the Videocon Group. The agency alleged that the petitioner had received an amount through a company where her husband served as a director, and that a flat was transferred to a Trust belonging to her husband. The petitioner filed a writ petition seeking to quash a sanction order dated May 15, 2023, granted under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act to prosecute her in a case registered by the CBI.

The petitioner argued that the Board of Directors of ICICI Bank does not possess the authority to grant sanction and that the RBI holds the power to remove an MD under the Banking Regulation Act. The advocate for the CBI argued that the Board of Directors held the power to appoint and remove an MD as per the Articles of Association, and that the question regarding the validity of sanction requires a trial and evidence for determination.

The court quashed and set aside the sanction granted by the Board of Directors, noting that the Board did not record the reasons in writing for the removal, and the document of sanction for prosecution issued by the Board dated May 15, 2023 did not constitute a sanction under Section 19(1)(c) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, resulting in the conclusion that cognisance taken by the court of the offence lacked basis relating to jurisdiction.

articles.title: Congress targets Modi government over inflation, seeks white paper on rising prices
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kharge says common person’s plate is getting smaller, pockets getting emptier, and making ends meet is getting harder

Accusing the Narendra Modi government of failing to control inflation, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) said the country's progress should be measured by the food on people’s plates and the money in their pockets, not the length of the Prime Minister's speeches.
His colleague and the party's communication chief, Jairam Ramesh, asked the Prime Minister to come out with a white paper on inflation.

“Modi ji promised to bring down inflation, but today the situation is such that the common person’s plate is getting smaller, their pockets are getting emptier, and making ends meet is becoming increasingly difficult,” Mr. Kharge said in a post on X.

Pointing to the rise in prices of essential commodities over the past 12 years, he said the cost of wheat flour had risen from ₹21 to ₹69 per kg, pigeon peas from ₹75 to ₹180, mustard oil from ₹102 to ₹263, and milk from ₹36 to ₹85.

“The measure of the country’s progress is not the length of your speeches, but the food on the common person’s plate and the money left in their pocket. How much longer will people keep paying the price for your economic mismanagement?” the Congress president asked.
Mr. Ramesh flagged the impact of rising prices on household budgets, citing reports of impending price increases in consumer goods ranging from smartphones and televisions to biscuits and salt.
He said companies were either raising prices or reducing the quantity in packets, leaving consumers with less for their money.

Retail inflation had reached 6.09% in October, with food inflation at 8.94%, while wholesale inflation stood at 12.29%, Mr. Ramesh said, adding that the latter was the highest under the current Wholesale Price Index series. He said that inflationary pressures were now affecting both household spending and production costs.

Citing a survey, he said 61% of households had seen their monthly expenditure on essential items rise by more than 20% over the past year, while 74% had been forced to cut down on non-essential spending.
He also flagged the possibility of higher equated monthly instalments following the Reserve Bank of India’s October increase in the repo rate.

articles.title: Bihar Legislative Council Secretariat rejects petitions seeking disqualification of two Independent MLCs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Opposition has earlier demanded that both be disqualified under the anti-defection law as they “joined” the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) after winning.

The Bihar Legislative Council Secretariat has rejected the petitions filed against two recently elected Independent Members of the Bihar Legislative Council — Bansidhar Brajwasi and Rahul Raj. articles.title: India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: While higher petroleum product exports offer a partial natural hedge, sustained increases in crude and gas prices could intensify pressure on the country’s import bill.

India’s crude oil import bill surged 87.5% year-on-year (YoY) to $19.5 billion in October, as elevated international benchmark prices, fuelled by renewed tensions in West Asia, sharply increased procurement costs. The increase came alongside an 11% rise in import volumes.

The net import bill, calculated as imports of crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas less exports of petroleum products, rose 60% to $16 billion during the month, compared with $10 billion in October last year.
Higher export realisations from petroleum products, however, provided some cushion against the escalating import burden.

According to provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), India imported 23.3 million metric tonnes (MMT) of crude oil in October, against 21 MMT in the corresponding month last year.
The expenditure on crude imports, meanwhile, climbed to $19.5 billion from $10.4 billion, reflecting the disproportionate impact of higher international prices on the country’s energy import bill.

The Indian crude oil basket averaged $119.91 per barrel in October, compared with $124.77 per barrel for Brent crude. In September, the Indian basket had averaged $116.09 per barrel, while Brent stood at $116.77 per barrel.

The sustained increase in benchmark prices, amid continuing geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia, has left India exposed to higher energy procurement costs, given its dependence on imported crude oil.
The impact of the rising crude import bill was partly offset by stronger earnings from petroleum product exports.
India’s petroleum product exports increased 5.9% in volume terms to 5.4 MMT in October. However, export revenues surged approximately 91% to $6.3 billion.
The increase in export earnings provided an important buffer against the higher cost of crude procurement.

articles.title: India-U.S. trade deal signing will still ‘take some time’, says Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: He added that the deal can be signed only after the U.S. finalises its new tariff framework. Recently, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the two nations had agreed that India would receive an advantage over its competitors

The actual signing of the India-U.S. trade will still “take some time”, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), adding that the negotiation part and the legal text will be completed soon.

The delay in signing, he said, was because it can be done only after the U.S. concludes its Section 301 investigations into its trade partners and finalises its tariff structure. A few days ago, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal asserted that the U.S. has acknowledged that India will receive lower tariffs as compared to its competitors.

“This is a deal that has been announced in February, the contours have already been announced as part of the joint statement,” Mr. Agrawal said while speaking at the curtain raiser of the FICCI Annual General Meeting. “The legal agreement has also been negotiated and it is now in final stages and it will be concluded soon.”
He was referring to the joint statement between India and the U.S. in February that announced the framework of an interim deal on trade.

However, Mr. Agrawal explained that the “challenge” is that this framework was announced against the background of the executive tariffs system that the U.S. President Donald Trump had put in place. At the time, the tariff on India was 50%. Later in February, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the legal foundation of these tariffs.

“Now a new tariff architecture is being created by the U.S.,” Mr. Agrawal explained. “So until that tariff architecture comes back in place, the signing of a deal is something that I think will take some time. But concluding the negotiations and having everything ready will be something that we will strive to achieve as soon as possible.”
In particular, Mr. Agrawal spoke about the investigations undertaken by the American administration under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

One of these investigations, regarding forced labour, has been completed and a tariff of 10% has been levied on imports from India. The second investigation, looking into excess capacity, is yet to be completed and could come with further tariffs.

“There are certain 301 investigations which are already under review,” Mr. Agrawal said. “Those will also be coming to the fore in the next few weeks or months. You can’t have a deal until you have got uncertainty around multiple investigations which are already there.”

Separately, without mentioning the U.S. or any other country, Mr. Agrawal also asserted that trade deals can take a long time to conclude when parties try to maximise the benefits accruing to them rather than engaging in a spirit of compromise.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance 📅 18 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 India-U.S. trade deal signing will still ‘take some time’, says Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

He added that the deal can be signed only after the U.S. finalises its new tariff framework. Recently, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the two nations had agreed that India would receive an advantage over its competitors

The actual signing of the India-U.S. trade will still “take some time”, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), adding that the negotiation part and the legal text will be completed soon.

The delay in signing, he said, was because it can be done only after the U.S. concludes its Section 301 investigations into its trade partners and finalises its tariff structure. A few days ago, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal asserted that the U.S. has acknowledged that India will receive lower tariffs as compared to its competitors.

“This is a deal that has been announced in February, the contours have already been announced as part of the joint statement,” Mr. Agrawal said while speaking at the curtain raiser of the FICCI Annual General Meeting. “The legal agreement has also been negotiated and it is now in final stages and it will be concluded soon.”

He was referring to the joint statement between India and the U.S. in February that announced the framework of an interim deal on trade.

However, Mr. Agrawal explained that the “challenge” is that this framework was announced against the background of the executive tariffs system that the U.S. President Donald Trump had put in place. At the time, the tariff on India was 50%. Later in February, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the legal foundation of these tariffs.

“Now a new tariff architecture is being created by the U.S.,” Mr. Agrawal explained. “So until that tariff architecture comes back in place, the signing of a deal is something that I think will take some time. But concluding the negotiations and having everything ready will be something that we will strive to achieve as soon as possible.”

In particular, Mr. Agrawal spoke about the investigations undertaken by the American administration under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

One of these investigations, regarding forced labour, has been completed and a tariff of 10% has been levied on imports from India. The second investigation, looking into excess capacity, is yet to be completed and could come with further tariffs.

“There are certain 301 investigations which are already under review,” Mr. Agrawal said. “Those will also be coming to the fore in the next few weeks or months. You can’t have a deal until you have got uncertainty around multiple investigations which are already there.”

Separately, without mentioning the U.S. or any other country, Mr. Agrawal also asserted that trade deals can take a long time to conclude when parties try to maximise the benefits accruing to them rather than engaging in a spirit of compromise.

articles.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for next U.S. House speaker
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Despite some opposition, Jeffries is expected to be elected speaker, a powerful position that puts him second in line to the Presidency, when the new Congress ‌convenes in early January

Democrats elected this month to the U.S. House ‌of Representatives nominated Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) to lead them in the next Congress, putting him ‌on the precipice of becoming the nation's first ‌Black ⁠House speaker.
The incoming House Democratic Caucus nominated Mr. Jeffries ⁠in a closed-door, secret-ballot vote.
Mr. Jeffries won 251 votes with 11 Democrats opposing him.

Many incoming progressives declined to say whether they would back Mr. ​Jeffries after the November ‌3 midterm elections, with several saying they wanted a leader who would support a bold agenda to pass populist policies that candidates campaigned on.
A group of seven ‌incoming House progressives said in a joint statement ​that they voted against Mr. Jeffries because they're still working to secure commitments from the New ⁠York Democrat.

"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the ‌direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of leadership," they said. "Those conversations are ongoing."

Despite some opposition, Mr. Jeffries is expected to be elected speaker, a powerful position that puts him second in line to the Presidency, when the new Congress ‌convenes in early January. The speaker election requires 218 votes on ​the House floor. Democrats will have a majority of at least 257 seats. Several competitive races ⁠remain uncalled.

House Republicans last week nominated Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan ⁠to lead their conference in January. Mr. Jordan won the post over Majority Leader Steve Scalise ‌after Speaker Mike Johnson said he would not seek to lead Republicans in the minority.

articles.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so

Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied to militias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray ‌region said, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals.

The build-up along the border has brought ​the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitors ACLED and the International ⁠Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray, and another person close to anti-government rebels there.

Reuters could not independently confirm reports of skirmishes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces along the border. ACLED and a person close to the rebels said the ‌two sides had clashed in recent days, which would be their first direct armed exchanges in over a month, but the person close to the pro-Ethiopian government militia disputed this.

Reached for comment, Eritrean Information ‌Minister Yemane Gebremeskel decried "propaganda" from Ethiopia's ruling party about developments near the border but did not directly address reports about ‌military ⁠build-ups or clashes.
Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Diplomats and ⁠experts have warned of possible conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea since fighting broke out in September between Ethiopia’s federal government and rebels in Tigray, which borders Eritrea.

Witnesses and Ethiopia's government said Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October in support ​of the rebels. ACLED reported at the time ‌that drone strikes it believed were carried out by Ethiopia’s military had targeted the Eritrean troops. Ethiopia has not commented on the strikes.

Eritrea has denied any incursion into Ethiopia and accused Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade its smaller neighbour, which was an Ethiopian province for three decades before gaining independence in 1993. They are now separated ‌by a border stretching more than 1,000 km (620 miles).

The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels. Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.

Ethiopia and Eritrea fought a border war from 1998 to 2000 that killed tens of thousands of people. The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory.

articles.title: U.S.-Saudi nuclear agreement 'satisfactory': IAEA
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: According to the accord, the IAEA "will be provided with information about, and access to any sites for conversion, enrichment, fuel fabrication and reprocessing" in Saudi Arabia, Grossi said
UN nuclear watchdog head Rafael Grossi on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) welcomed a deal between the United States and Saudi Arabia on equipping the kingdom with a civilian nuclear programme.
The deal announced in July has provoked questions about the risks of nuclear proliferation.
"It's a very satisfactory outcome that we have with this agreement," Mr. Grossi told reporters after opening an International Atomic Energy Agency board of governors' meeting.
Once nuclear power development gets under way in Saudi Arabia, "we will be there," he added.

In his opening statement, Mr. Grossi told the board that the United States and Saudi Arabia in October requested the IAEA "to take the necessary steps to implement safeguards and verification measures" for their agreement.
According to the accord, the IAEA "will be provided with information about, and access to any sites for conversion, enrichment, fuel fabrication and reprocessing" in Saudi Arabia, Mr. Grossi said.
"I welcome the open, transparent approach and engagement of both governments with member states and the secretariat on this matter," he added.
Mr. Grossi told reporters the agreement was "fully aligned with the legal framework that we have at the IAEA".
He added Saudi Arabia had also agreed to "additional verification measures on a voluntary basis".
U.S. media have reported the agreement would allow Washington to export technology without the usual safeguards preventing future military use.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

According to the accord, the IAEA "will be provided with information about, and access to any sites for conversion, enrichment, fuel fabrication and reprocessing" in Saudi Arabia, Grossi said

UN nuclear watchdog head Rafael Grossi on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) welcomed a deal between the United States and Saudi Arabia on equipping the kingdom with a civilian nuclear programme.

The deal announced in July has provoked questions about the risks of nuclear proliferation.

"It's a very satisfactory outcome that we have with this agreement," Mr. Grossi told reporters after opening an International Atomic Energy Agency board of governors' meeting.

Once nuclear power development gets under way in Saudi Arabia, "we will be there," he added.

In his opening statement, Mr. Grossi told the board that the United States and Saudi Arabia in October requested the IAEA "to take the necessary steps to implement safeguards and verification measures" for their agreement.

According to the accord, the IAEA "will be provided with information about, and access to any sites for conversion, enrichment, fuel fabrication and reprocessing" in Saudi Arabia, Mr. Grossi said.

"I welcome the open, transparent approach and engagement of both governments with member states and the secretariat on this matter," he added.

Mr. Grossi told reporters the agreement was "fully aligned with the legal framework that we have at the IAEA".

He added Saudi Arabia had also agreed to "additional verification measures on a voluntary basis".

U.S. media have reported the agreement would allow Washington to export technology without the usual safeguards preventing future military use.

articles.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa says both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests
India and Canada could be announcing a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s official visit in December, according to the country’s High Commissioner to Ottawa, Dinesh K. Patnaik.
Both countries are also in the final stages of negotiations of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. “We are on the cusp of finalising it,” Mr. Patnaik said.

Addressing a gathering in the Canadian capital organised by the Centre for Strategic Statecraft and the Canadian International Council, he said that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests.

Mr. Patnaik took over as India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa in September 2025. Both countries had earlier expelled each other’s High Commissioners and reduced their diplomatic presence following the murder of Sikh Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June 2023. Then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused India of orchestrating the murder, throwing bilateral relations into a tailspin. Subsequent reports by Canadian agencies also listed India, alongside China and Russia, as an interferer in domestic politics. The turnaround in ties, which began with the mutual reinstatement of High Commissioners, is set to reach a milestone with Mr. Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12.

Mr. Patnaik said India and Canada are no longer talking about a reset of their derailed relations, but rather an overarching boost in ties spanning defence, space, nuclear energy, deep tech, trade, and the mobility of people. The two nations have moved from a complete lack of trust over a year ago to an unprecedented degree of mutual trust, he added.

“The fact is that in the core strategic concerns of Canada and India, there is no conflict. Still, all it took for the entire bilateral relationship to be derailed was the fringe diaspora issue,” he said, referring to the murder of Nijjar.

“The reason was the lack of trust. India believed that Canada was actively promoting separatism in India, and Canada believed India was organising violence in Canada. We had a series of meetings between senior Ministers, NSAs of both countries, and agencies at all levels as we set about rebuilding trust. Today, we have reached the highest levels of trust, where the most sensitive areas of cooperation, such as deep tech, defence, and space, are subjects of mutual cooperation,” Mr. Patnaik said.
Cooperation between Canadian and Indian agencies remains at a high level, the High Commissioner added.

articles.title: India sitting on 'economic disaster': Rahul Gandhi at Columbia University
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: At Columbia University, Congress leader questions fairness of electoral process, speaks on manufacturing decline; links U.S. midterm setback to erosion of American power

Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said the country’s economic model ceased to deliver results nearly a decade ago, leaving it with a deepening employment crisis and a weakened manufacturing base.

Speaking at a fireside chat at Columbia University on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), moderated by New York Times journalist Lydia Polgreen, Mr. Gandhi said India is sitting on an “economic disaster” that could become far more serious if the country continued on its present course.
“The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That’s the reality of it,” he said.

“One can brush it aside, the media can brush it aside. But India has got a massive unemployment problem. India’s got a massive problem with its education system. And these are things you cannot get away from,” he added.

Mr. Gandhi identified small and medium businesses, agriculture and manufacturing as the backbone and principal engines of job creation, arguing that the services sector could not absorb India’s expanding workforce.

“The spine of the economy is small and medium business, which is the job creation engine, and agriculture. That is fundamental in India and required. The spine of the economy has been broken,” he said.

The Opposition leader said India could not achieve sustainable economic development without rebuilding its manufacturing capabilities. “We cannot survive successfully without manufacturing, it just cannot be done,” he said.
Mr. Gandhi alleged that economic growth was concentrated in a few large business groups while smaller enterprises were struggling.

“Why is there no private investment in India? Why are the only people who are growing in India, businesses that are growing in India called Adani and Ambani? Why is Tata literally being taken over by Mr. [Gautam] Adani?” he asked.

Mr. Gandhi placed the recent student-led Gen Z protests alongside resistance movements by Adivasis, Dalits and farmers against what he called the growing concentration of political and economic power in the last decade. He said the student-led protests showed that fear of “coercive power of the State” didn’t work.

articles.title: Researchers boost gut microbial activity linked to longevity in aged mice, find improved metabolism
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier ageing

Researchers have identified changes in the metabolic activity of the gut microbiome associated with exceptional longevity in humans, and found that amplifying the same activity in aged mice using engineered bacteria improved metabolic health.

Published in the journal Cell Metabolism , the team's study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier aging.

Senior author Amir Zarrinpar, chair in circadian biology and medicine, and professor of medicine at the University of California San Diego, said while many studies on aging focus on what goes wrong as one grows old, the findings suggest "some changes in the gut microbiome may actually represent the body's attempt to preserve metabolic health".
"If we can identify those beneficial functions and safely strengthen them, we may eventually be able to develop new ways to promote healthier aging," Zarrinpar said.

The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria and other microbes living in the digestive tract, is known to change throughout life and plays an important role in metabolism and inflammation, among other aspects of health.
Studies have also found distinctive microbiome features among people who age exceptionally well.
The researchers focused on how gut microbes modify bile acids, substances produced by the liver that help digest fats but also act as signalling molecules in the body.

Studying young and aged mice, they found that aging was associated with an increased microbial activity linked to enzymes called bile salt hydrolases. These enzymes chemically modify bile acids, allowing them to influence pathways involved in metabolism, inflammation and the body's internal clock.
The team also found greater bile acid modification in the mice.
To determine patterns in humans, they reanalysed publicly available data from a human ageing cohort, analysing bile acid measurements from 48 young adults, 107 older adults and 125 centenarians.

articles.title: Does India need to financially aid families’ decisions to have a child through fertility treatment?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Indian laws protect the decision not to have a child through statutes, schemes and subsidies, but the decision to have one is left to the mercy of the private assisted reproduction healthcare market

The reproductive-autonomy jurisprudence as evolved by the Supreme Court under Article 21 of the Constitution is rich yet narrow, focusing primarily on one side of the problem. In Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), the Court held that reproductive choices may be exercised to procreate as well as to abstain from procreating. In X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department (2022), the Supreme Court extended the right to abortion to unmarried women as an exercise of ‘decisional autonomy’.

These, and nearly all other landmark cases are concerned only with an existing pregnancy. The freedom to pursue parenthood through medical treatment, however, has surfaced only at the margins. The Delhi High Court, in 2023, allowed parole of a life convict to attempt IVF, by recognising a “right to parenthood,” but only as a claim against a barrier the State itself had erected. No court has yet asked whether the State may leave a citizen’s access to infertility care entirely to their own purse. Can a right available to the fertile but structurally withheld from the infertile be called a universal right?

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days.

On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri.

Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year .

When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay.
“El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said.

During El Niño years, the northeast monsoon tends to be significantly more active over southern peninsular India. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas.

And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.

Mr. Ramakrishna also pointed out that in October and November, the Bay of Bengal consistently retained high sea surface temperatures—over 26.5 degrees Celsius—and anything above 26 is conducive to developing a cyclonic system. This has been aided by the El Niño-modified upper-level wind patterns over the southern Bay of Bengal, which reduce vertical wind shear.

Another key factor that acted as a catalyst is the massive freshwater discharge from rivers like the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Godavari into the Bay of Bengal, which resulted in creating a low-salinity surface layer. This acts as a “barrier layer” that prevents cooler, deeper ocean water from mixing upward, so a passing cyclone (like Arnab or Murasu) does not cool the sea surface enough to stop the next storm from forming days later.

Persistent upper-tropospheric ridges (anticyclonic circulations) over the China–Myanmar region and central India have acted as steering barriers, blocking storms from recurving northeast and forcing them northwestward into the Andhra coast, he said.

articles.title: Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks

Demand for air purifiers in India has witnessed explosive growth in 2026, with major brands and retail platforms reporting sales doubling or tripling year-on-year. Driven by an early surge ahead of the traditional winter pollution season , consumer behaviour is shifting toward viewing indoor air quality as a year-round health priority rather than an emergency seasonal purchase.
According to industry leaders, adoption is gaining momentum well before peak pollution months.

Smart tech brand Qubo recorded a 150 percent growth over the previous year, while Xiaomi registered approximately 3X year-on-year sales growth during the festive period. Industry executives note that growing awareness surrounding indoor pollutants, ranging from dust and pet dander to everyday cooking and cleaning emissions, is encouraging households to take a proactive approach to home wellness throughout the year.

Retail footprint and online traffic reflect this expanding market footprint across the country. Electronics retailer Croma reported that air purifier sales volumes have more than doubled in 2026. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks.
Premium tech maker Dyson also reported that visits to its air purifier pages grew by over 100 percent in October compared to the same period last year.

Modern buyers are increasingly seeking advanced functionality and intelligent filtration tech. Croma highlighted strong consumer interest in models featuring real-time AQI displays, app controls, and multi-functional units combining purification with humidification or heating.

On e-commerce platforms, Amazon India reported that sales doubled over the past week. Shoppers are actively leveraging Rufus, Amazon’s personalised AI shopping assistant, to filter models by room size, filter type, and live sensor capabilities, prompting the e-retailer to expand selection on Amazon Now for immediate delivery.

“We have observed a notable increase in consumer demand for air purifiers on Flipkart, reflected in higher search activity, product discovery and purchases. Northern India continues to account for a significant share of demand for the category. We also witnessed a rise in purchases during the early hours following Diwali, coinciding with heightened concerns around deteriorating air quality and the steps households are taking to manage their indoor environments,” said Flipkart.

fullParagraphs: The robotic probe, launched in 1977, was calculated by NASA to have reached a light-day from Earth, ‌the distance that light travels in 24 hours — about 26 billion km

NASA’s Voyager 1 probe is believed to have now ​hit a distance milestone accomplished by no other spacecraft from Earth, based ⁠on advance computations by the U.S. space agency, as the probe ventures through the near-emptiness of interstellar space.

The robotic probe, launched in 1977, was calculated by NASA to have reached a light-day from Earth, ‌the distance that light travels in 24 hours — about 16 billion miles (26 billion km) — on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at 5:16 a.m. ET (1016 GMT).
Infographic | Voyager I — A five-decade journey to get one light-day away

Officials at NASA’s Jet Propulsion ‌Laboratory in California will have to wait about a day to get a ‌signal ⁠from the probe, confirming it has reached this distance. They have scheduled an event ⁠for Thursday (November 19) to discuss the milestone.
“Reaching one light-day is an astounding feat, one that I never expected to see,” Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd said.

Voyager 1, the most distant human-made object, is flying at almost 38,000 ​miles per hour (61,000 kph). It crossed ‌the outer edge of the heliosphere, a protective bubble of particles and magnetic fields produced by the sun, to enter interstellar space in 2012. Its twin, Voyager 2, was also launched in 1977 and entered interstellar space in 2018.
A Jet Propulsion Laboratory representative ‌said recent power-saving measures could give the two Voyager spacecraft enough power to stay in ​communication with Earth for three to four more years.

“But the goal of the mission is to do science, and there is enough power to ⁠keep the current suite of instruments going through the 50th launch anniversary next year. Beyond that is hard to predict, and of course these are nearly 50-year-old spacecraft, and there are ‌always things the team cannot anticipate that might happen,” the JPL representative said.

Voyager 1 journeyed past Jupiter and Saturn, the solar system’s two largest planets, earlier in its mission. It continues to gather scientific data. For instance, its instruments have detected the faint monotonous hum caused by the constant vibrations of the small amounts of gas present in interstellar space.

“Voyager is sending back continuous measurements of magnetic fields, cosmic rays and of plasma waves that we ‌receive on Earth whenever the Deep Space Network points its antenna at Voyager,” Mr. Dodd said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sakuntala Narasimhan, a trailblazing musician, journalist, feminist and consumer rights activist, passed away on November 18. She was 86.
A multifaceted personality, she had the rare distinction of being a vocalist in both Carnatic and Hindustani traditions, apart from being a journalist with two PhDs in Women’s Studies and Musicology.

When her first-born was only a year or two, she mysteriously lost her voice. She could barely speak, let alone sing. The doctors failed to identify the cause. For Sakuntala, an accomplished vocalist, being confined to home with a young child and unable to sing was deeply frustrating.
It was this setback that led her to take up writing, recalls her daughter, Shobhana Narasimhan, professor at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research.

“A women’s magazine held a short story competition, which she won. She then got to know the people at the magazine and gradually started writing more and more,” her daughter recollected. She was a longstanding columnist for multiple newspapers.

“When she got married, she was pursuing a PhD in economics. However, she couldn’t complete it because I was born a year later. It always bothered her that she didn’t have a PhD,” says Ms. Shobhana, a physicist.
“When I got my PhD in 1991, I told her, “Amma, now it’s your turn.” She went ahead and got her first PhD in women’s studies and then another in musicology.”
Sakuntala Narasimhan with musician Archana Udupa. | Photo Credit: File photo

Renowned musician Archana Udupa, one of her students, remembers her as a genius who could do self jugalbandi, switching back and forth between Hindustani and Carnatic styles. She however, feels her teacher didn’t get the dues she deserved.

“She was the only A-top artist — A Top is more than A grade — in both All India Radio and Doordarshan, and both in Carnatic and Hindustani. I think our industry could have celebrated her even more. She got her State award when she was nearing 80. We need to celebrate such people at the right time and before it is too late.”

articles.title: Shiv Sena members tear pages of Sonia Gandhi’s book over Savarkar references, seek ban in Maharashtra
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party has demanded that publisher HarperCollins withdraw two pages from the memoir, while the Congress condemned the protest and Uddhav Sena leaders hit back at the Shinde faction

Members of Shiv Sena on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) tore pages from Sonia Gandhi's memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love, demanding that the publisher withdraw two pages that the party claimed contained objectionable references to Vinayak Damodar Savarkar.

“We have torn the pages of the book as a mark of protest against the statements on Savarkar ji. We have sought that Harper Collins, the publisher, should scrap these two pages. Till they do that, we have sought that the Maharashtra government ban the sale of the book in the State. We will soon write to the government to seek a ban,” Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Nirupam told The Hindu .
He was among the six party spokespersons who addressed a press conference on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). The Shiv Sena is part of the ruling Mahayuti alliance in Maharashtra.

The Congress hit back at the Sena, condemning the act as “shameful”. “It shows intellectual bankruptcy. I feel pity for them. When you spit at the sun, the spit lands on you. It is a condemnable act,” Maharashtra Congress president Harshawardhan Sapkal said.

Former Chief Minister Prithviraj Chavan termed the act “childish”. “We are not the Taliban. We believe in the Constitution of Babasaheb Ambedkar. Everyone has the right to express their opinion. If you do not accept her views or if you think there are factual inaccuracies, refute them or point them out or write a separate book. But tearing a book is childishness,” he said.

Meanwhile, Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC tore a photograph bearing the image of Balasaheb Thackeray during the press conference. When this was pointed out to her, she was seen slipping the torn photograph under a pile of papers. She later justified the act, saying that the photograph showed Balasaheb Thackeray slapping an effigy of Manishankar Aiyar with a chappal.

“This is what he has taught us. We have only torn the pages of a book,” she said. She was later summoned by Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. After the meeting, he said there was no question of anyone insulting Balasaheb Thackeray.
“He is venerable for us. Nobody can insult him,” Mr. Shinde said.

Meanwhile, the Uddhav Sena staged protests at several places in Maharashtra, including Mumbai. The issue also triggered a backlash in the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), where Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Kishori Pednekar engaged in a heated exchange with Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde.
The Shiv Sena said the references to Savarkar appeared on pages 201 and 443 of the book.
